They need linen as well to make their first true mage's robes. Undercity initiates gather a bolt of simple linen and potent Dalaran mana gems for their first true robes. Those robes mark their station and personal worth. Anastasia Hartwell directs the novices to gather the raw materials for an enchanted weave. The mana gems cannot be bought or conjured. Dalaran mages are stationed across Silverpine Forest, especially near Ambermill, and the gems must be taken from them. Anastasia Hartwell says Dalaran's arcane philosophies mirror those of the Forsaken. Yet sentiment has no place in the Undercity. To the Forsaken, wizards too weak to defend their relics forfeit their treasures and their lives. Josef Gregorian is a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where the gathered cloth and gems are brought. He lacks the magical talent to judge the pristine quality of Dalaran's enchanted stones. But he has the rare artisan skill to weave their raw power into the robes.

quest:1962.text: Spellfire Robes. In the Undercity, Spellfire Robes mark a young Horde mage's passage toward mastery. Josef Gregorian finishes them after the apprentice brings rare components from across the realm. In Lordaeron, you need more than ordinary cloth to channel and shield your growing magic. Josef Gregorian is a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. He makes magical garments from specialized materials gathered by promising Horde spellcasters. The final stitching marks your passage beyond basic incantations toward arcane and fire magic. Josef Gregorian needs alchemical and arcane components to make robes that focus powerful magic. You gather the supplies through dangerous trials and bring them to his sanctum in the Undercity. There, Gregorian weaves them together. The robes mark your growing status and offer protection as an aspiring mage.

quest:1963.text: The Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, Therzok tests rogues who seek entry to the secretive Shattered Hand. Their trial sends them after Tazan, a troll smuggler, and his locked satchel. The Shattered Hand works from the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. This order of assassins and thieves keeps to old orcish traditions. Warchief Thrall rules the young Horde with honor, diplomacy, and caution. Yet the Shattered Hand's leaders believe restraint weakens their people, so they seek to restore martial supremacy through covert violence. They use knives and poison when a battlefield charge may fail.

quest:1978.text: The Deathstalkers. In Undercity, the Deathstalkers welcome a new operative into their ranks. You carry Andron's Ledger to Varimathras as proof of the Syndicate's covert work. Mennet Carkad welcomes you into the Deathstalkers after you uncover Andron Gant's records. The order serves Lady Sylvanas across Lordaeron as her eyes, ears, and daggers. Its agents use intelligence, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to remove threats before they rise. Recognition by the order marks your first step in service to the Forsaken. You deliver the sensitive ledger to Varimathras in Undercity's Royal Quarter. The nathrezim commander oversees Forsaken tactical intelligence under Sylvanas Windrunner. Pleased by the Deathstalkers' initiative, Varimathras welcomes your ability and says his intelligence division can use someone who delivers results.

quest:199.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, sabotage threatens the barrier that holds back Loch Modan's waters. You find a barrel near the shore and bring its strange smelling powder to Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh. Whispers of sabotage have reached the shore around the Stonewrought Dam. Near the water's edge, a barrel lies where it does not belong. Inside is strange, pungent powder, far from the dam's maintenance supplies.

quest:1998.text: Fenwick Thatros. In the Undercity, Mennet Carkad sends promising rogues to kill Fenwick Thatros on Lord Varimathras's orders. Thatros is suspected of gathering independent undead along Silverpine Forest's shores. His death proves an operative's mettle to the Deathstalkers and earns access to advanced trade training. In the Undercity's Rogues' Quarter, Mennet Carkad handles Deathstalker contracts and trains rogues. The Deathstalkers are the Forsaken's secretive intelligence wing. Lord Varimathras has named Fenwick Thatros a priority target, a charge too serious for novice recruits. Thatros has established a foothold among rogue undead in Silverpine Forest. Left alone, their independent leaders could threaten Forsaken control across Lordaeron's old holdings. Deathstalker scouts place Fenwick Thatros near a decrepit dock on Lake Lordamere in Silverpine Forest. To reach him, you must cross wilderness claimed by feral beasts, Rot Hide gnolls, and Scourge remnants. Varimathras demands proof of the kill: Thatros's severed head. Bring it back, and you may earn entry into deeper covert operations.

quest:2038.text: Bingles' Missing Supplies. On Loch Modan’s southeastern shore, Bingles Blastenheimer is stranded after troggs steal his gear. You can recover his tools and Blastencapper explosives so he can repair his gyrocopter and return to the fight for Gnomeregan. Bingles Blastenheimer crashes his gyrocopter into Loch Modan’s cold waters. He drags himself ashore, dazed, and troggs from the lake’s central islands swarm him. They steal his most valuable belongings. Troggs scatter Bingles’ gear among their island camps. The stolen things include a wrench, screwdriver, and hammer, along with his volatile, high-yield invention, the Blastenheimer Blastencapper. Left among troggs, the explosives put travelers in immediate danger. Bingles fights to free Gnomeregan, his homeland, from subterranean troggs and irradiated leper gnomes. He imagines a decisive aerial assault, but without his tools and Blastencappers he cannot rebuild his flying machine. His campaign remains grounded in the reeds.

quest:2039.text: Find Bingles. In Ironforge, Gnoarn starts a search for Find Bingles after more than a week without word. Bingles Blastenheimer vanished during a flight toward fallen Gnomeregan, and searchers are sent to Loch Modan's shores. There, Bingles is alive and needs mechanical salvage. Gnome aviator Bingles Blastenheimer was sent from Tinker Town in Ironforge to scout the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan from the air. More than a week has passed without word. Gnoarn fears Bingles may have blown himself out of the sky, a danger of gnome engineering. His last report placed him somewhere above Loch Modan's waters. Searchers find Bingles alive along the Loch Modan shoreline, far from a tragic pile of wreckage. He is unfazed by his long absence and takes slight offense that anyone doubted his piloting. Rather than return promptly to report to Gnoarn, he asks his rescuer to recover tools and Blastencapper explosives stolen by troggs. He wants them so he can resume his duties for the gnomish movement.

quest:2041.text: Speak with Shoni. In Ironforge, Alliance travelers are sent to Stormwind to find Shoni the Shilent, whose unit prepares for Gnomeregan. After Gnomeregan fell to radiation, surviving gnomes made an exile quarter in Ironforge. Its engineers, tinkers, and strategists keep seeking a way back into their lost home. Tinkertown directs the effort, but the preparations reach beyond Khaz Modan. Now adventurers are sent south to Stormwind, where military gear for fighting underground is being prepared. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent commands an elite crew trained for underground assault. Her sappers need gyrodrillmatic excavationators to burrow toward the sectors held by troggs. The Deeprun Tram runs beneath the mountains between Ironforge and Stormwind, making the journey to Shoni straightforward.

quest:2118.text: Plagued Lands. Darkshore's wildlife is falling to a creeping sickness, and Tharnariun Treetender seeks a way to save it. He asks you to calm a rabid thistle bear with an enchanted relic and bring it back alive. A creeping sickness twists Darkshore’s beasts into maddened, violent creatures. Thistle bears suffer most, and their frenzy threatens travelers and the coast’s fragile balance. Night elf sentinels answer with steel, while druids seek to understand the sickness and heal its cause. Tharnariun Treetender will not kill the corrupted beasts before trying to save them. He made a trap called Tharnariun’s Hope. Set on the forest floor, its soothing light briefly calms a raging thistle bear. Pacified, the bear follows you back to Tharnariun’s outpost for study.

quest:2138.text: Cleansing of the Infected. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender asks you to stop the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cleanse one failed, and he fears the rabid beasts will harm other creatures and spread the sickness. Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness in Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. So he asks you to put them down before they maul other creatures or carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

quest:2139.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turn. Travelers have put down infected beasts across Darkshore, and now he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of town. Since the Third War, an unnatural sickness has made Darkshore's wild creatures rabid. Tharnariun Treetender is stationed in Auberdine, where he has asked travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. Yet killing rabid thistle bears treats only a symptom. Tharnariun decides the source among the local bears must be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother. Tharnariun gives profound thanks after the Den Mother's death, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agony. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. Auberdine's defenders accept the heavy burden of protecting their wilderness.

quest:214.text: Red Silk Bandanas. In the Deadmines, Scout Riell sends the People's Militia after Red Silk Bandanas. Their fine weave marks the Defias leaders directing the uprising in Westfall. Scout Riell and the People's Militia have learned that cloth marks rank in the Defias Brotherhood. Across Westfall, common cutpurses and highwaymen tie coarse red cloth over their faces. Senior conspirators and inner-circle operatives wear fine red silk. Recovering their bandanas strikes at the experienced officers coordinating Edwin VanCleef's uprising. The senior outlaws gather deep in the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook. Sentinels and scouts outside Sentinel Hill depend on freelance champions to enter the contested tunnels. Each silk bandana recovered means one fewer lieutenant organizing ambushes, guarding weapon caches, or enforcing VanCleef's rule across Westfall.

quest:217.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. Captain Rugelfuss sends you into Stonesplinter Valley to stop the attacks on the King’s Lands. Scouts have traced them to Grawmug, chieftain of the Stonesplinter troggs. His death may break the pack’s resolve and help reclaim southern Loch Modan. Captain Rugelfuss’s scouts have found that the Stonesplinter troggs follow Chieftain Grawmug. Their attacks threaten the King’s Lands in southern Loch Modan. You are sent into their lair to kill Grawmug and his personal bruisers. Breaking the pack’s cohesion may stop its advance. Grawmug holds a cavern in the southeastern cliffs of Stonesplinter Valley. His trusted brutes, Gnasher and Brawler, stand beside him, making the three a danger to a lone soldier. Defeating them could throw the remaining troggs into disarray. That would give the beleaguered Mountaineers time to fortify the roads and drive the beasts back underground.

quest:2178.text: Easy Strider Living. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong offers hunters her own recipe for strider stew if they bring her foreststrider meat. Auberdine's coastal folk make use of the wildlife around them. Alanndarian Nightsong has her own recipe for hearty strider stew, made from the tall foreststriders that range through Darkshore's woods. She asks you to hunt the birds and bring back their meat before she shares her cooking. Foreststriders range through the woodlands and beaches north and south of Auberdine. Their sharp beaks and quick tempers make them dangerous when provoked, but their meat makes a rich stew. Bring fresh meat to Alanndarian, and she will share her recipe.

quest:22.text: Goretusk Liver Pie. At the Saldean Farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean is making pie through hard times. Bandits have ravaged the kingdom’s breadbasket, and homesteaders hunt aggressive boars to feed their families. Westfall once fed Stormwind as its fertile breadbasket. Now neglected roads, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields make life hard for the few settlers who remain. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works to keep a sense of home despite the dangers. A traditional meat pie offers one of the few comforts to homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life. Goretusks roam Westfall’s plains in great numbers. Their tough hides and vicious tusks make them dangerous to farmhands alone, yet their meat feeds families cut off from regular trade. Salma’s recipe calls for crushed rosemary, minced garlic, chopped dill, and simmering gravy. Prepared with care, the beasts’ pungent organs become a rich, savory meal.

quest:224.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the southern watchtower, Mountaineer Cobbleflint calls for help as Stonesplinter troggs press toward the Valley of Kings. Ironforge’s forces serve on distant fronts. Cobbleflint and the guards are too few to stop the growing trogg invasion beneath the great dwarven monuments. King Magni Bronzebeard has sent much of his regular army abroad to support the Alliance. Local patrols and hired blades must keep the province from being overrun. Stonesplinter Valley cuts through Loch Modan’s southern peaks, where troggs have burrowed up from the depths. Their scouts reconnoiter the roads while warriors build camps along the valley floor. If left unchecked, their parties threaten the roads to the southern passes. The Mountaineers must fight them without pause.

quest:2259.text: Erion Shadewhisper. From the forests of Teldrassil, promising rogues are sent to Darnassus. At the Cenarion Enclave, Erion Shadewhisper points them toward work beyond the forests. Jannok Breezesong sends you from Teldrassil to find Erion Shadewhisper in Darnassus. There is no need to fear a summons to Syurna, the exacting trainer. Erion waits in the Cenarion Enclave, where he handles work that calls for a quieter touch. For rogues in night elf lands, Teldrassil's forests can no longer contain their duties. Erion Shadewhisper sends capable hands into a wider, more dangerous world. Their work lies across the sea.

quest:2260.text: Erion's Behest. In Darnassus, Erion Shadewhisper sends promising night elf rogues across the Great Sea. He sees their growing skill in stealth and directs them to Stormwind City to report to Stormwind Intelligence. Night elf rogues train in Teldrassil's shadow under mentors such as Erion Shadewhisper. When one shows exceptional talent, word travels beyond the World Tree. Through Erion, Stormwind Intelligence, also called SI:7, invites you across the Great Sea to the human capital. From northern Kalimdor, you travel by way of the docks at Darkshore or the Wetlands to Stormwind City. In the capital, you make your way to SI:7 headquarters in Old Town and report to Renzik "The Shiv." He assesses newcomers and opens the way to advanced espionage, poison mastery, and covert operations for the Alliance.

quest:2281.text: Redridge Rendezvous. In Lakeshire, promising Alliance rogues train for dangerous work under seasoned operatives. SI:7 sends them east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to prepare for the field. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, knows that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. So SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains. There, Lucius trains them among Lakeshire’s docks. Lakeshire gives Lucius good ground for clandestine training. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the frontier town. Its piers let him test a rogue’s stealth, reflexes, and lockpicking without drawing the notice of townspeople or guards.

quest:2300.text:
SI:7. From Goldshire, promising young rogues are sent to report to Renzik "The Shiv" in Stormwind. There, you enter Master Mathias Shaw's service, where covert work awaits. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius watches Goldshire's local recruits. You prove cunning and capable against the growing Defias threat, and Sylvius passes along a message from headquarters. Report to Renzik "The Shiv" without delay. You leave Elwynn's fields for Stormwind's covert ranks. Behind an unassuming barracks in Old Town, Stormwind's hidden agency keeps its headquarters. Master Mathias Shaw commands its work across the kingdom and beyond. The agency handles covert operations, reconnaissance, and assassination.

Renzik "The Shiv" is Shaw's sharp-tongued second-in-command. He assesses promising agents, then sends them into dangerous work beyond the reach of the kingdom's formal military.

quest:237.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. In southern Loch Modan, Mountaineer Gravelgaw calls for help against the Stonesplinter troggs. With dwarven forces committed to the Alliance front, local outposts rely on volunteers to hold the line. The Mountaineers guarding the southern pass into Dun Morogh are stretched thin. King Magni Bronzebeard has sent much of Ironforge's strength to the wider Alliance front, leaving the Valley of Kings towers short of regular infantry. So Mountaineer Gravelgaw calls on volunteers to strike Stonesplinter Valley and keep the troggs at bay. Reinforcements may never come. The Stonesplinter troggs are neither mindless nor aimless. Their war bands fight with brute force and crude elemental magic. Gravelgaw wants their veteran Skullthumpers and their Seers, who lead with mystic power, driven from the fight. Without those leaders, the tribe's southern camps lose their order and cannot mass against the Ironforge road.

quest:2378.text: Find the Shattered Hand. A Forsaken rogue from Tirisfal Glades is bound for Orgrimmar, where the Shattered Hand awaits. The Deathstalkers send the promising initiate across the sea to Durotar to learn the clan’s specialized arts. Mennet Carkad has seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken train their own covert order, the Deathstalkers. Their alliance with the Horde opens a path to darker arts. So Mennet directs promising rogues to the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, joining Lordaeron’s undead operatives with Kalimdor’s orcish assassins. The journey ends beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow. Warlocks, rogues, and demon-binders work out of sight there. Shenthul, a Shattered Hand trainer, awaits the newly arrived undead agent. The gruff troll greets the envoy with harsh skepticism. Reputation alone will not satisfy him; he wants to see whether the envoy has real cunning or has wasted the voyage across the Great Sea.

quest:2379.text: Zando'zan. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul sends a promising rogue to meet Zando'zan. There, training begins for the Shattered Hand's covert ranks. Orgrimmar's rulers know strength alone cannot win every war. Beneath the city, the Cleft of Shadow is home to the Shattered Hand, a covert guild serving the Horde through espionage, sabotage, and theft. When rogue trainer Shenthul sees promise in an initiate, he sends them to Zando'zan for training as an operative. Zando'zan tests each inexperienced rogue who enters the cavern before granting respect. Meeting him begins formal training in stealth, subterfuge, and thievery. His lessons bridge the gap between rough street cutpurses and organized intelligence operatives. From there, rogues prepare for fieldwork beyond the safety of the capital's red canyon walls.

quest:2380.text: To Orgrimmar!. Kaplak sends a young rogue from Razor Hill north to Orgrimmar. You are to find Shenthul in the Cleft of Shadow and enter the Shattered Hand's network. Kaplak sends you north from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Your growing skill has drawn the notice of handlers with greater standing, though your craft is still rough. You leave Durotar's red crags behind and make for the capital.

quest:2381.text: Plundering the Plunderers. Near Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives in Ratchet. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor. Southsea Freebooters crew the ship. Rogues must board unseen and enter the pirates’ den, where cutpurses train. Then they pick the strongboxes in the hold and bring back the plunder.

quest:2382.text: Wrenix of Ratchet. In Orgrimmar, Wrenix of Ratchet draws Horde rogues toward a goblin port far to the south. Zando'zan sends you to aid Wrenix the Wretched, a disreputable goblin in Ratchet. In the Cleft of Shadow, Orgrimmar's rogue guild works from winding crevices, mostly unseen. Zando'zan is a troll who greets operatives with wild ramblings and dark portents. He speaks of Warchief Thrall struck down by poison and blade. Then he gives no reason for the vision and sends agents south to Ratchet, a port town in the Barrens. Ratchet lies on the Barrens coast, east of the Crossroads. Scoundrels, mercenaries, and tinkerers gather in this neutral port, where Wrenix the Wretched makes his home. Wrenix has little patience for Zando'zan's strange ways. He says the troll's earlier recruits met grim ends in the bay, among its hungry predators.

quest:244.text: Encroaching Gnolls. Gnolls press toward Redridge’s western road, and Lakeshire fears being cut off. Guard Parker spots camps near the border and sends word to Deputy Feldon. The warning confirms the town’s fear that the beastmen may isolate Redridge. Guard Parker watches the western border trail, where the road leads from Elwynn Forest into Redridge Mountains. Stormwind’s forces have thinned, leaving few defenders along the route. Parker keeps the gravel road open for supply wagons, but his scouts report gnoll warbands advancing from the crags to the north and east. Their camps lie alarmingly close to the road. Near the Lakeshire bridge, Deputy Feldon receives the warning and sees the danger facing the town. Redridge gnolls raid near Lakeshire, while their camps near the Elwynn border could let them encircle the town and push into the kingdom’s heartland. Stormwind has ignored pleas for reinforcements, leaving Lakeshire’s watch unready for threats from both sides.

quest:246.text: Assessing the Threat. Near Lakeshire, Deputy Feldon needs to learn how great the gnoll threat has grown. With the garrison stretched thin and Stormwind withholding reinforcements, he pays travelers to thin the packs and gauge their strength. Blackrock orc warbands threaten Lakeshire from the heights, while aggressive gnolls roam the valleys. The town has too few defenders for ordinary scouting patrols. When reports showed gnolls pressing toward the border, Deputy Feldon called on travelers. He pays them to test the enemy in the wild, sparing guards the town cannot afford to send. You scout along Redridge's southern road and strike the camps of Redridge Mongrels and Poachers. Each fight thins the gnolls' forward scouts and disrupts their supply lines. The clashes reveal whether the packs are scattered scavengers or an organized force threatening Lakeshire. Feldon can use what you learn to plan the town's strained defense.

quest:250.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh fears Dark Iron sappers near the eastern ramp threaten the Stonewrought Dam. With much of its garrison sent to the Alliance Front, you investigate the danger. The Stonewrought Dam holds back Loch Modan's waters. Ironforge engineers raised it as a great work, yet much of its security detail has gone to the Alliance Front. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh and his small crew now have little protection if an attack comes. Dark Iron dwarves struck the Thandol Span and pillaged Dun Modr in the Wetlands. Now known sappers lurk near the dam's eastern ramp. Hinderweir fears the clan has turned to Loch Modan's lifeline, and means to demolish it.

quest:2518.text: Tears of the Moon. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Once blessed by Elune, the spider now brings danger, and the Sisterhood seeks to ease her suffering and recover her sacred spinnerets. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Elune once blessed the spider. Beneath the night sky, Sathrah wove silver webs across Teldrassil's boughs, and evening mist gathered on them. The Sisterhood of Elune collected the shimmering dew for its healing power in sacred rites.

quest:2520.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah a final rite. You bring her spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters, where the Priesthood seeks to cleanse her soul of corruption. Priestess A'moora asks you to perform a final rite for Lady Sathrah after she is slain. The dark madness spreading across Teldrassil twisted the great spider's peaceful nature into mindless aggression. The Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence, not treat her death as a simple culling. You place her silvery spinnerets in the fountain at the heart of the Temple of the Moon. Its consecrated waters wash away the corruption and grant her release.

quest:255.text:
Mercenaries. In Thelsamar, Magistrate Bluntnose hires passing fighters as Mo'grosh ogres press into northeastern Loch Modan. Ironforge has promised soldiers for the valley's defense, but they are months away. Settlements, excavations, and the Stonewrought Dam remain exposed. Ironforge took two months to promise a handful of soldiers for Loch Modan's local defense. Another two months will pass before they arrive. Thelsamar's guards are stretched thin as hostile forces gather beyond the valley. Magistrate Bluntnose cannot wait for reinforcements. Mo'grosh ogres have fortified a camp in the hills northeast of the loch. Their growing presence threatens Thelsamar, the Ironband Excavation Site, and the Stonewrought Dam. If the dam is attacked or damaged, destruction downstream would be catastrophic.

Without official mountaineer detachments, Bluntnose hires independent fighters to thin the ogre ranks. He hopes to buy the valley time against both ogres and troggs.

quest:257.text: A Hunter's Boast. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling sets you a timed hunt in Loch Modan: bring down six mountain buzzards within fifteen minutes. Daryl calls himself Daryl the Bold and dismisses travelers as greenhorns who cannot match his hunting skill. Then he points you toward the mountain buzzards scavenging around the lodge's nearby crags and hillsides. The hunt tests your speed, patience, and aim against the buzzards' quick flight. Bring down all six before time runs out, and Daryl grudgingly gives up one of his ranged weapons. He offers you further hunting dares, too.

quest:258.text: A Hunter's Challenge. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling dares you to kill five elder mountain boars within twelve minutes. He expects Loch Modan's rough highlands and dangerous wildlife to make you fail. Daryl the Youngling lives among Farstrider Lodge's seasoned huntsmen, but he lacks their quiet patience. He covers his youth with bluster and long hunting tales, including rambling accounts of how he earned his “famous” scar. He refuses to admit that anyone else is skilled. He also keeps getting his fellow hunters' names wrong and sets strict trials for newcomers, hoping to humble them and restore his standing among the lodge's residents. Elder mountain boars roam Loch Modan's crags and hillsides. They are massive and thick-skinned, and grow dangerous when provoked. Daryl gives you twelve minutes to find and kill five. If you finish in time, the loudmouthed youngster retreats awkwardly and pretends he knows nothing of the extravagant wager he made so casually.

quest:26.text: A Lesson to Learn. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, an elder of the Cenarion Circle guides their first steps toward aquatic form. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and is ready for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them to master the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus. To cross the depths without drowning, young druids need the guidance of the Cenarion Circle’s elders. You leave Darnassus for Moonglade, an ancient sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze waits as an elder mentor of the Cenarion Circle. Starblaze judges whether young shapeshifters are ready for the trials that lead to aquatic form. Mastering water takes physical resilience and mental resolve.

quest:263.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the Southern Guard Tower, Mountaineer Wallbang calls travelers to defend Loch Modan from the Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's reserves sent to distant fronts, the southern pass is thinly held. Wallbang sends seasoned recruits into Stonesplinter Valley against the clan's shamans and bonesnappers. Loch Modan's defenses are stretched thin. Ironforge's regular reserves have been summoned to distant fronts across Azeroth, leaving the Southern Guard Tower short-handed. Mountaineer Wallbang and his few comrades face constant pressure from the Stonesplinter clan. They depend on Alliance travelers passing through to help hold the southern pass. The fight reaches beyond stray scouts to the Stonesplinter clan's strength. Its bonesnappers bring brutal force, while its shamans use earthen magic to rally their kin. Slaying twenty of these foes weakens the clan's incursions into the lowlands. It also serves King Magni Bronzebeard's defense of the realm.

quest:264.text: Until Death Do Us Part. In Silverpine Forest, Clarice Foster sends her keepsake to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to lay it on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children. Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage with bitterness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead. He declared service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away. Yuriv’s tomb lies in the graveyard around the Sepulcher, marked by gashes, rubbish, and weeds. Set Clarice’s pendant on the relief of his sculpted hands. No grand magic or spiritual closure follows. The gem grows dull, and a cold, silent gust passes over the tombs. The old resentments of Lordaeron’s fallen people remain.

quest:267.text: The Trogg Threat. At Loch Modan’s Southern Gate, Captain Rugelfuss faces a growing trogg threat with too few defenders. The Ironforge Reserve has been called away to Alliance battlefronts, leaving him to hold the pass while troggs threaten the nearby hills. Dwarven mountaineers and the Ironforge Reserve have gone to reinforce Alliance battlefronts. Captain Rugelfuss now has only a small garrison. Strict orders keep him at the gate, unable to lead an attack into the highlands. Settlers and travelers there remain exposed to ambushes. Troggs in the nearby crags threaten Khaz Modan. Left unchecked, their numbers grow quickly, and they could overrun dwarven outposts. Rugelfuss calls for help to buy time and thin their ranks. Strike at the troggs in their hillside warrens, then bring back their stone teeth as proof.

quest:27.text: A Lesson to Learn. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids north to study the waters. Their road leads to Nighthaven in Moonglade, where the Cenarion Circle guides their training. You have learned the bear form and its strength. Now Turak Runetotem turns his students toward adaptability. Azeroth's waterways hold hazards that are hard for travelers bound to land. So he sends those devoted to nature north to learn the aquatic form. Turak Runetotem sends you beyond Mulgore to learn how to shape yourself for the waters. You travel to Moonglade, the sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal, and reach Nighthaven. There, night elf mentors of the Cenarion Circle welcome tauren students. They set factional strife aside to preserve the shared teachings of Cenarius. Dendrite Starblaze waits for you in Nighthaven, where your training begins. The night elf elder says mastery over the waters must be earned. Two trials await. One tests your endurance and composure beneath the water. The other calls for deep spiritual understanding of the aquatic aspect.

quest:272.text: Trial of the Sea Lion. Druids in Moonglade seek the sea lion’s spirit through a sacred rite. They recover two scattered pendant halves for agility and endurance, then unite them at the Shrine of Remulos to prepare for Aquatic Form. Druid initiates in Moonglade undergo trials of attunement as they prepare to navigate Azeroth’s deep waters. The Trial of the Sea Lion follows earlier preparations in their spiritual training. Dendrite Starblaze oversees it in Nighthaven, where initiates learn to balance the sea lion’s graceful speed with its resilient stamina. Both are needed to take its form and withstand the ocean depths. The trial centers on reuniting the two halves of the Pendant of the Sea Lion. One represents the sea lion’s agility as it glides through turbulent currents. The other represents its endurance, the fortitude to dive long into freezing water without faltering. Initiates seek guidance from Moonglade’s inhabitants as they search across the world for the scattered relics. Once both halves are found, the initiate brings them near the Shrine of Remulos, where they can be joined into one talisman. The shrine’s energies bind agility and endurance in harmony. The initiate then presents the restored pendant to Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. With the pendant, the druid shows readiness to embrace the sea lion aspect and awaken Aquatic Form.

quest:273.text: Resupplying the Excavation. Jern Hornhelm sends you from Thelsamar after a slow wagon carrying blastpowder to Ironband's Excavation Site. Its three dwarven haulers travel south along the Loch's shore. In southern Loch Modan, Ironband's Excavation Site needs blastpowder to break through hard rock. The powder comes first to Thelsamar, where Jern Hornhelm arranges for Huldar, Miran, and Saean to haul three volatile barrels south. The heavy load slows their pack team along the lakeside road, giving you time to catch them and help on the way.

quest:274.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At Stonewrought Dam, strange powder puts Loch Modan and Ironforge at risk. Ashlan Stonesmirk in Dun Modr identifies it as unstable Seaforium, which can explode when it touches water. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognizes the silver crystals and sharp odor in samples from Stonewrought Dam. The powder is Seaforium. It stays inert while dry, but moisture makes it react violently. An unchecked blast could blow Ironforge out of the mountain, Ashlan warns.

quest:2751.text: Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks an apprentice to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks a budding smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar beneath the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, so he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward. Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury. Its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meet his demands, and he may believe an apprentice can keep the Omosh legacy alive and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

quest:2753.text: Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh tests smiths with hard work. Green iron armor puts their endurance to the proof and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, while the Omosh bloodline's techniques hang in the balance. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar with trials of hard physical labor. To him, metalworking is more than heating ore and shaping it. It honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and making tempered green iron armor again and again builds muscle and discipline. Smiths who bring Orokk the requested green iron gear win rare praise from the gruff armorsmith. He compares an artisan who endures the work to his grandfather, Chief Gorokk of Omosh. For the armor, Orokk teaches the ancestral design for sturdy iron boots. Horde warriors wear them to crush their enemies beneath their heels.

quest:2755.text: Joys of Omosh. After your great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith wipes his tears away as soot, then dances for joy to pass on an unusual piece of family heritage. At Orgrimmar's forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. Your great help has touched the burly blacksmith deeply. Yet he stubbornly blames a fleck of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping. Before you part, Orokk Omosh says he must share one last family secret. He performs the vigorous, exhausting Omosh dance of joy for his apprentice. Then he teaches the apprentice to strike with an iron fist.

quest:278.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron explosives threaten the Stonewrought Dam, and Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs your help. He asks you to gather rare reagents from Loch Modan so he can make a mixture to neutralize them. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs three ingredients for his mixture. Forest Lurker venom, a tear from a crocolisk in the Loch, and a Mo'grosh crystal each bring a different reaction. Together, they can render the dwarven charges inert. The ingredients lie in dangerous parts of Loch Modan. Forest Lurker spiders and crocolisks threaten travelers, while Mo'grosh ogres guard their mined crystals in a stronghold to the northeast. Reaching the crystals means facing the ogres in their encampments.

quest:280.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron saboteurs threaten the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs the charge disarmed before the loch floods the lowlands. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh saw Dark Iron Insurgents swim toward the Stonewrought Dam with a keg of explosive Seaforium. No Mountaineers were nearby to stop them. The infiltrators fastened the keg against the dam’s underwater foundation. If the dam breaks, the loch will flood the lowlands and cripple dwarven trade and travel.

quest:29.text: Trial of the Lake. In Moonglade, an initiate faces the Trial of the Lake, a timed test of speed and dexterity. You dive into Lake Elune'ara for an unstable Shrine Bauble, then hurry to the Shrine of Remulos before it decays. Success earns Tajarri's recognition and honors the Cenarion Circle's devotion to balance. Moonglade's guardians oversee this rite for initiates. You dive into Lake Elune'ara to find a delicate Shrine Bauble resting along the sunken lakebed. It begins to decay as soon as you disturb it, so you need a sure touch, keen senses, and swift movement to carry it overland before its magic fades. Once you have the bauble, you must hurry to the Shrine of Remulos in northwestern Moonglade. The monument honors Keeper Remulos, who guides the Cenarion Circle in preserving nature and world balance. Activating the bauble there marks its importance to the Circle. Warden Tajarri greets initiates who beat the time limit and the competition.

quest:2948.text: Gnome Improvement. In Ironforge, Talvash del Kissel offers to improve a ring he made in Gnomeregan. He needs silver and moss agate for a delicate lattice over its old band. Talvash del Kissel fled Gnomeregan after the trogg invasion and radiation brought the city down. Now the gnome refugee lives in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The jeweler and tinkerer is short on coin and out of stock, but determined to prove his skills remain sharp in exile. Talvash is glad to see his simple ring design again, cleaned by the Sparklematic 5200. Yet he considers the old band dated. He offers to improve it with silver and moss agate lattice work, showing his skill with metal and gemstones.

quest:2950.text: Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg seeks to improve a ring brought from Gnomeregan. He wants rare materials and word of the Dark Iron dwarves, hoping to prove goblin craft finer than gnomish design. You carry a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer studies its plain gnomish work and offers a bargain. Bring him raw materials and a small fee, and he will frame the band with silver and moss agate. The lattice is meant to strengthen the magic within.

quest:297.text: Gathering Idols. At an excavation site, troggs clutch the carved idols Magmar Fellhew seeks. The relics have driven them into a violent frenzy. Researchers uncovered a large cache of strange, carved stone idols shortly before savage troggs surfaced and overran the excavation site. The attack drove the expedition from the ruins before any formal study could begin. Now the troggs clutch the relics and prowl the site, barring a peaceful return. The troggs seem deeply affected by the idols, beyond merely taking them. Their strange carvings exert an unsettling power that drives the creatures into an uncontrollable rage. Magmar Fellhew wants to study the idols safely and quell the frenzy gripping the area, so he seeks to take them from trogg hands.

quest:298.text: Excavation Progress Report. At Ironband's Excavation Site, Prospector Ironband needs you to carry his dispatches and powder orders to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar. Ironband's dispatches tell of his dig and renew its supply requests. The work needs picks, workers, and blasting powder to break through bedrock. Ironband relies on runners to keep Jern Hornhelm informed.

quest:2997.text: Tome of Divinity. Azar Stronghammer sends promising dwarven paladins from Dun Morogh to Ironforge for deeper instruction. There, Tiza Battleforge awaits in the Hall of Mysteries, where the trials begin in service to the Holy Light. Dwarven initiates guard Dun Morogh's snowbound villages and roads. When Azar sees that a defender is ready for deeper spiritual instruction, he sends that candidate from field duties to Ironforge. There, the city's holy elders can guide them. The summons takes you through the Mystic Ward to the Hall of Mysteries. Sacred relics and solemn study fill its halls. Tiza Battleforge tests your readiness for self-sacrifice, mercy, and the moral duties of your calling.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons now calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Brother Wilhelm sends for them, and the Tome of Divinity begins the sacred trials that teach mastery of resurrection through the Holy Light. In Elwynn Forest, novice paladins spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows discipline in battle and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. The paladin leaders mark promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind. Their report is due at the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the kingdom's foremost sanctuary for its priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall lives there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set the formal trials of the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The trials test compassion, fortitude, and willingness to sacrifice.

quest:2999.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, young dwarven paladins are sent to Tiza Battleforge to learn the Holy Light's deeper duties. Their rite of passage reaches beyond martial training and toward sacred vows. You have defended Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls, proving your discipline in battle. Now Brandur Ironhammer, your trainer, sends you upstairs in the Hall of Mysteries. Senior paladins there prepare initiates for the order's spiritual duties. Tiza Battleforge teaches that the Light asks more than swordplay and hammer blows. It asks for compassion, justice, and self-sacrifice. Seeking her begins your formal study of the Tome of Divinity, a sacred path toward the power to resurrect the fallen.

quest:3000.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, dwarf paladins return for deeper training in the Holy Light. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker sends them home, and Tiza Battleforge guides them toward the sacred trials of the Tome of Divinity. Dwarf paladins keep their spiritual and martial roots in Khaz Modan, even when they serve Stormwind or travel through human lands. When Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker judges that a dwarf has gained enough field training, he sends them home. There they learn the duties expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand. In Ironforge, you are directed to the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Mysteries. Tiza Battleforge waits upstairs, where she mentors young dwarven paladins. She prepares them to bear the burden of the Holy Light through sacred trials recorded in the Tome of Divinity.

quest:301.text:
Report to Ironforge. Jern Hornhelm sends Ironband’s report to Prospector Stormpike in Ironforge. The dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies, and the Explorers’ League must attend to it. The Explorers’ League funds and oversees archaeological expeditions across Khaz Modan, and supplies them. Ironband’s dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies. Its overseers cannot simply requisition more nearby.

At the Thelsamar inn, Jern Hornhelm entrusts you with Ironband’s written report. You carry it over the mountain passes to Prospector Stormpike at the League’s headquarters in Ironforge.

quest:302.text: Powder to Ironband. In Ironforge, the Explorer's League sends blasting powder south to Prospector Ironband's dig in Loch Modan. Prospector Stormpike approves the request, and the shipment goes to Thelsamar before continuing to Ironband's Excavation. The Explorer's League sends blasting powder from Ironforge to Prospector Ironband's expedition in southern Loch Modan. When the dig runs short, word reaches the League's leaders. Prospector Stormpike approves the request and sends the runner to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar, the valley's main supply hub.

quest:307.text: Filthy Paws. In Silver Stream Mine, Filthy Paws supplies wait in danger. The Miners' League stored its equipment there after the ore ran dry, but kobolds now fill the tunnels. Mountaineer Stormpike wants the tools recovered before his warriors attack. Silver Stream Mine lies in northern Loch Modan, east of Algaz Station. Its silver ran out long ago, so the dwarven Miners' League turned the empty shafts into a depot for spare excavation gear, picks, and staging materials. Across Khaz Modan, sturdy tunnels make good storehouses, provided they stay guarded and locked against the wilderness. As dwarven watchfulness across Loch Modan has thinned, kobolds have slipped into the mine. Dark shafts and gleaming iron tools drew the scavengers, and soon the depot became their warren. Mountaineer Stormpike is ready to lead warriors inside and drive them out, but their heavy boots and sweeping blows could smash the crates. You can slip or fight your way in to recover the League's supplies before the assault begins.

quest:309.text: Protecting the Shipment. In southern Loch Modan, Miran carries blasting powder toward Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband needs it for his dig, but failed supply lines and threats to the courier wagons have left Miran stranded. Prospector Ironband needs blasting powder to cut through stone at his dig. Miran is stranded on the road under threat, carrying a heavy load. You guide him along the uneven roads to the excavation site so the powder can reach the dig.

quest:31.text: Aquatic Form. In Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to be recognized among the keepers of nature. The druid has proved worthy in Moonglade and taken on the sea lion aspect; now formal recognition brings Aquatic Form. Dendrite Starblaze sends you back to Mulgore after your trials in Moonglade. The Pendant of the Sea Lion bears proof of your balance and dedication across Kalimdor's waters. By carrying it home, you show that you have honored the ancient traditions needed to take an aquatic aspect. At Thunder Bluff's heights, you bring the pendant to Turak Runetotem, your mentor. He is pleased that you have honored your ancestors and kept nature in balance. Then Turak teaches you the secret of aquatic form. You can swim beneath rivers and oceans, breathe freely, and find your way through the depths as a sea creature.

quest:312.text: Tundra MacGrann's Stolen Stash. Tundra MacGrann needs his winter stores back from Old Icebeard. The yeti carried off the thorium-reinforced meat locker, and MacGrann's injured leg keeps him from reaching the cave. For the cold season, MacGrann had salted away a month's worth of dried meat. He sealed it in a thorium-reinforced locker to keep hungry bears out. Old Icebeard carried off the whole chest instead of trying to open it. While MacGrann was away hunting deer, Old Icebeard dragged the chest to a cave in the jagged hills. MacGrann believes the yeti cannot break through solid thorium, but his injured leg keeps him from retrieving the stores. You can face the beast or slip inside while it prowls the snowdrifts.

quest:314.text: Protecting the Herd. At Amberstill Ranch, Rudra Amberstill fears Vagash will take more prized mountain rams. He asks passing fighters to protect the herd and bring proof of the predator’s death. Vagash has taken two prized mountain rams from Amberstill Ranch. The ranch supplies the Bronzebeard dwarves with riding and working beasts, and the herd supports Dun Morogh’s rustic economy. Vagash hunts local livestock in the crags above the ranch. Ironforge’s forces are spread thin across the realm, supporting the Alliance on distant frontiers. With no military patrol on the ridgelines, Rudra Amberstill asks independent fighters to hunt Vagash. He wants one of the beast’s deadly fangs as proof.

quest:3221.text: Speak with Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel awaits your findings about the tainted wolf hearts. High Executor Hadrec has sent you to speak with the Royal Apothecary Society researcher. After you help the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec gives you an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has studied discolored wolf hearts gathered from local wildlife and needs you at once. Apothecary Renferrel works for the Royal Apothecary Society in a laboratory inside the Sepulcher crypt. He studies how dark magic and disease are changing Silverpine's beasts. His alchemical research draws on military reports from the front.

quest:3261.text: Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, Jorn Skyseer guides Horde hunters seeking deeper knowledge of the wilds. After your hunts for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker teaches you more. You have hunted sunscale and scytheclaw raptors across the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows a hunter needs more than skill with weapons; the land's great beasts demand understanding. Her teaching here is done, so she sends you south. The Gold Road leads south across rougher plains to Camp Taurajo, a tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker with lessons for hunters who seek elusive and legendary quarry across the Barrens.

quest:3281.text: Stolen Silver. At the Crossroads, Gazrog sends you after silver stolen from the guards’ payroll by raptors. Their cunning has led you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and raptors have taken their wages. He sends you to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. At first, he wanted vengeance for the ambush on the payroll shipment. But killing the pack would not bring the money back. The Horde needs to learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin and where they took them. Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory and guard it beside their eggs and fresh kills. Gazrog's tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.

quest:3301.text: Mura Runetotem. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Mura Runetotem hopes a shell from the Barrens can help the Forsaken. Around the Barrens oases, Tonga Runetotem studies wildlife changed by magic. The altered snapjaws catch his eye. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. So he asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms. At the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest, Mura Runetotem aids her allies. She made the arduous journey to help them cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. The shell holds an inner glow and an enduring spark of life. Mura hopes it may reveal how to restore vitality to the northern continent.

quest:3524.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, sea creatures are washing ashore in growing numbers. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde studies the deaths from Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Great sea creatures have sometimes beached themselves on Darkshore. It is a tragic sight, but it has been occasional. Now they wash ashore in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon fear these deaths may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor. The Temple of the Moon sends scholar Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to the port town of Auberdine to learn why the great beasts come ashore. Based there, she gathers biological samples to send by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. Greymist murlocs swarm the carcasses in the surf, scavenging the remains. Without armed protection, researchers cannot reach the bones.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. From Stormwind's Dwarven District, the road reaches an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. In Ironforge, the Stormpike clan is respected for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore entrusts travelers with carrying the weapon north, across the distance from Stormwind to the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. Rumors of unrest and banditry reach the southern human kingdoms, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:354.text: Deaths in the Family. In Brill, Coleman Farthing seeks vengeance on the Agamand family. He once worked at their mills and stayed to defend their estate during the Third War. His fellow workers and their stubborn masters died there, then rose as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential farming family. Their mills and fertile pastures yielded grain through the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crossed Lordaeron, the family refused to flee or leave its ancestral lands. They believed their stone walls and loyal workers could hold back the horrors advancing from the east. Coleman Farthing and the other workers trusted their lords' assurances and stayed to defend the estate. The Scourge overwhelmed them. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered, then raised into undeath where they fell. Farthing eventually broke free through Sylvanas Windrunner's liberation. The Agamand patriarchs and heirs remained under the Lich King's mental grip, wandering the ruined mills as mindless Scourge sentries. Coleman Farthing now lives in Brill, still bitter toward the masters whose pride cost him his mortal life. Seeking vengeance and closure, he sends Forsaken champions to Agamand Mills to destroy Gregor, Nissa, and Thurman Agamand. He hopes his former masters kept enough awareness behind their rotting faces to feel terror as their unlife came to an end.

quest:356.text: Rear Guard Patrol. At the Bulwark, Deathguard Linnea sends you to guard Tirisfal's eastern flank. Scourge horrors and lingering spirits threaten Balnir Farmstead, the road, and the supply lines that keep the front supplied. The Bulwark guards Tirisfal Glades from the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands. Deathguard Linnea watches over the defenders behind the frontier. They cannot spare troops to guard against attacks from the rear. So any undead that slip past the choke point must be destroyed before they cut the supply lines feeding the front. Balnir Farmstead once worked as a farm in eastern Tirisfal, but fell to ruin during the Third War. Blight covers its fields, and Bleeding Horrors and restless Wandering Spirits shelter in its crumbling stables. Clearing the farmstead denies the Lich King a place to gather forces inside Tirisfal. It also keeps the road open for Horde reinforcements.

quest:3681.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Master Brandur Ironhammer sends promising human paladins south for deeper training. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Master Duthorian Rall guides their study of the sacred Tomes of Divinity. Stormwind calls promising holy warriors south to the Cathedral of Light. Senior priests and paladin mentors await them there, keeping the Silver Hand's traditions alive in the Church of the Holy Light among human lands. Master Brandur Ironhammer knows when a student is ready for deeper study of the faith. You can reach Stormwind's Cathedral District by the Deeprun Tram or across the mountain passes. There, Duthorian Rall prepares initiates to study the sacred Tomes and learn the rites of redemption.

quest:369.text: A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan searches old records for a plague that endured in spider venom. He hopes to give the Forsaken a potent new biological agent. Apothecary Johaan studies old texts in Brill for the Royal Apothecary Society. There he finds records of an ancient pestilence that killed thousands. The writings say its pathogen endured across generations in the venom of spiders native to Tirisfal Glades. Johaan needs that venom as a biological reagent. Apothecary Johaan sends agents to eastern Tirisfal Glades in search of a living sample. Venomweb Vale lies south of the Scarlet Monastery, and vicious night web spiders fill its hollow. To gather fresh venom glands for Johaan's experimental brew, harvesters must enter the spiders' dens.

quest:372.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, Executor Zygand sends Forsaken agents from Brill against the Scarlet Crusade. Captain Melrache and his sworn guards hold a ruined watchtower beyond Faol's Rest. The Forsaken are securing Lordaeron's ruins, but the Scarlet Crusade keeps testing Tirisfal's borders. From a tower in the north, past Faol's Rest, crusaders lead raids against Forsaken patrols and lands. Executor Zygand means to strike the officers directing those raids before another attack comes. Captain Melrache commands the northern camp with two sworn bodyguards always at his side. From the tower, the Scarlet Crusade watches the coastal roads and nearby woods. Kill Melrache, and the raiders near Brill lose their order. His fall removes a direct threat to Lady Sylvanas's young kingdom and drives the zealots toward stronger fortifications farther east.

quest:3741.text: Hilary's Necklace. At Lakeshire's docks, Hilary loses the necklace her father gave her. Shawn asks you to find it in Lake Everstill, where their parents forbid them to swim. Hilary and Shawn fish from Lakeshire's docks, seeking an ordinary day amid the threats around the Redridge Mountains. Then Hilary's treasured necklace slips into Lake Everstill. They search the piers and shore, but find nothing. Shawn asks you to help. Their parents forbid Hilary and Shawn to swim in Lake Everstill. Aggressive murlocs and hungry threshedons lurk below the surface. The necklace lies in glinting mud at the lake bottom, beyond the children's reach. So Shawn asks you to recover the gift.

quest:38.text: Westfall Stew. On her farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers face bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a meal that sustains her farmhands. Salma's recipe brings together local okra, stringy meat from circling vultures, and snouts from wild goretusks roaming the plains. It also calls for fresh murloc eyes gathered from coastal raiders. Such fare may turn delicate stomachs in Elwynn, but Westfall cooks swear the blend makes a rich, fortifying meal.

quest:385.text: Crocolisk Hunting. At Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart seeks trackers to hunt Loch Modan's crocolisks. Their hides and meat bring steady trade, though hunting along the lake's shores and rocky islets is dangerous. Crocolisks haunt the shallows and muddy banks, making crossings and fishing perilous. Across Khaz Modan, craftsmen and tailors seek their hides for rugged armor and leather goods. Rustic taverns pay well for the lean tail meat. Loch Modan's crocolisks gather mainly around the rocky islets. Their crushing jaws and sharp teeth make them dangerous quarry. Dwarven veterans like Marek Ironheart carry scars from wrestling them into submission. He warns that one misstep in the water can cost a limb. Skinning and butchering one takes patience, sturdy steel, and a willingness to enter its hunting ground.

quest:3921.text: Wenikee Boltbucket. Near the Mor'shan Rampart, Sputtervalve needs Wenikee Boltbucket to mend a broken samophlange. He damaged it after it was retrieved from the Sludge Fen, and now his claims to his colleagues in Undermine hang on its repair. Sputtervalve's claims to his fellow engineers in Undermine rest on a broken machine. An adventurer retrieved the mysterious samophlange from the Venture Company's control console at the Sludge Fen. Sputtervalve could not resist showing it off, and his tinkering damaged the delicate contraption. Now he needs someone with sharper skill to find the fault and repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket camps beside the road just south of the Mor'shan Rampart, which divides the northern Barrens from Ashenvale. Her curious mind is drawn to intricate machinery, and the broken samophlange quickly catches her attention. Its inner gears fascinate her, so she sets to work figuring out how to rebuild it.

quest:3922.text: Nugget Slugs. At the Sludge Fen, Wenikee Boltbucket seeks parts for a samophlange she has recovered. She sends you to the nearby Venture Company crews for spare hardware. Wenikee Boltbucket has recovered a samophlange and wants to learn how its intricate workings fit together. The goblin machine needs exact parts, so she sends you to the Venture Company crews at the Sludge Fen. Their heavy tool buckets hold the seventeen-point-five gauge nugget slugs she needs.

quest:3923.text: Rilli Greasygob. Wenikee Boltbucket sends a damaged samophlange to Rilli Greasygob in Orgrimmar. She hopes his knowledge of its Venture Company origins will explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed it was close to collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone who knew its design. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Wenikee sends you to Nogg's Machine Shop. Rilli Greasygob works there as an engineer and once learned his trade within the Venture Company. He recognizes the machine at once and marvels that anyone survived exploring the company's contested operations in the Barrens.

quest:3924.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob needs help with a broken samophlange. The goblin engineer sends you back into the Barrens for the operating instructions, held by his former Venture Company rival. Rilli Greasygob once worked beside Boss Copperplug in the Venture Company. Copperplug oversaw the samophlange’s inner workings and guarded their secrets closely. He gave Rilli no manual. Instead, Copperplug handed separate pages only to underlings he trusted, leaving his fellow engineer without the knowledge to understand the device.

quest:399.text: Humble Beginnings. In Cathedral Square, Baros Alexston asks you to search his family's burned farm in Westfall. Thieves hold the ruins, and he hopes to recover the compass he treasured as a boy. Baros Alexston once worked the fields of Westfall. Now he is Stormwind City's accomplished architect, advising on stonework and city buildings. Few in the kingdom have made such a journey from farm to city. Yet Baros remains bound to the humble beginnings that shaped him. Lawlessness swept across Westfall and reached the Alexston Farmstead. Bandits and vagrants burned the house, driving Baros's father from his livelihood. Family heirlooms remained behind amid the fire and occupation. Now Baros asks you to search the ruined, bandit-held farmstead west of Sentinel Hill for his first compass, hidden before the home fell.

quest:408.text: The Family Crypt. Scourge forces press the Forsaken at Agamand Mills. From Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends agents to strike the undead in the family crypt. The Forsaken hold Tirisfal Glades, though the Scourge still commands much of its countryside. The Agamand Mills once ground flour for Lordaeron. Now the mills shelter the Scourge. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren watches the enemy gather with grave concern. Every stretch of land lost to the undead weakens the Forsaken's independence. Captain Dargol, a skeletal commander, has made the Agamand Family Crypt his headquarters. He uses necromancy to raise generations of the Agamand dead as Rotting and Wailing Ancestors, swelling his ranks. Magistrate Sevren sends Forsaken agents to purge the crypt and lay its disturbed dead to rest. He also wants Dargol's head, to disrupt Scourge forces in northern Tirisfal.

quest:409.text: Proving Allegiance. Gunther Arcanus tests whether you serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. He sends you to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a Scourge operative near his island. Gunther Arcanus has lived on an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath. He guards his freedom fiercely. Bethor Iceshard enchanted Gunther's spellbook and found no Scourge taint on the emissary. Yet neither words nor charms can quiet Gunther's suspicions. He needs an outsider to prove hostility toward the Lich King's minions through decisive violence before he will trust them.

quest:411.text: The Prodigal Lich Returns. In the Undercity, you carry a Nether Gem to Bethor Iceshard after winning Gunther Arcanus's trust and restoring his grimoire. Gunther Arcanus spent years alone on an island in Brightwater Lake. By will alone, he escaped the Lich King's control, not knowing Sylvanas Windrunner had freed Lordaeron. Bitter and wary, he distrusted the Undercity's emissaries. An adventurer returned his spellbook and showed him their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied the visitor was no enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to contact his former colleague.

quest:416.text: Rat Catching. In the western foothills, tunnel rat kobolds trouble the roads into Thelsamar. Mountaineer Kadrell calls on travelers to drive them back and bring proof of the cull for a bounty. West of Thelsamar, tunnel rat kobolds have made dens in the foothills of Loch Modan. They foul the surrounding ground and trouble the roads leading into town. Their warrens threaten the safety and cleanliness of those roads. Mountaineer Kadrell has set a bounty on the tunnel rat kobolds. He asks passing travelers to bring their severed ears as proof of the cull. Then he pays coin and compensation, though the trophies are foul to inspect.

quest:417.text: A Pilot's Revenge. Hildelve’s search ends in the crags of Dun Morogh, where Pilot Hammerfoot’s searchers find him frozen beside his journal. His last words call for vengeance. Hildelve’s journal tells of his savage fight with Mangeclaw, the huge Ice Claw bear. He drove the beast away at first, but his wounds were grave. Mangeclaw returned and killed him. Hildelve’s final plea calls for vengeance against Mangeclaw. Bring his journal and a claw torn from the beast to Pilot Hammerfoot. The grim news gives the Ironforge Siege Brigade closure and honors its lost comrade.

quest:418.text: Thelsamar Blood Sausages. At Thelsamar's Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove keeps Thelsamar Blood Sausages on the table. A favorite across Loch Modan, they need fresh ingredients from the valley. Hungry children and miners returning from the Ironband Excavation fill Thelsamar's tavern. Vidra Hearthstove tends the stove, making sausages known across Loch Modan. Her recipe draws on wildlife from the rugged mountain pass. Vidra uses boar intestines for casings and bear meat for the filling. Spider ichor gives the sausages their sharp, pungent bite. Gathering the entrails and venomous fluid takes a steady stomach, though travelers come to appreciate this regional favorite.

quest:422.text: Arugal's Folly. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver sends Forsaken agents to a nearby farmstead for Arugal's earliest spellbooks. The Forsaken need to understand the magic behind the worgen curse if they are to turn it against Arugal and secure Silverpine Forest. The Remedy of Arugal is the first step in unraveling the threat from Shadowfang Keep. In the Sepulcher's crypts, ambitious Forsaken mage Dalar Dawnweaver holds Archmage Arugal in contempt. He sees him as an ordinary practitioner whose place in the Kirin Tor makes no sense, and whose grasp of magic seems amateurish. Yet the monstrous beasts roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver means to take apart the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

quest:423.text: Arugal's Folly. In Silverpine, Forsaken agents seek shackles worn by Moonrage worgen. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's notes to learn how the renegade mage strengthened his unstable magic. The bindings may help the Forsaken break the worgen threat. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's recovered research and speaks of his former peer with open contempt. He says Arugal was unfit to serve Dalaran, let alone wield high sorcery in the kingdom's darkest hour. Short on talent, Arugal turned to enchanted relics and devices to strengthen and bind the worgen he summoned. Dalar needs samples to study the magic that tethers the beasts. Moonrage worgen roam Silverpine wearing shackles marked by Arugal's binding enchantments. Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls prowl north and east of the Sepulcher. Their heavy metal shackles hold residual arcane energy. Dawnweaver hopes that energy will help him find a way to counter Shadowfang Keep.

quest:424.text: Arugal's Folly. Worgen hold Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine's southeastern hills, keeping the Forsaken from ore needed by Varimathras's forces. Dalar Dawnweaver sends you to slay their corrupted foreman, Grimson the Pale, and carry his head to the Sepulcher. Dalar Dawnweaver learns from the Forsaken Darkstalkers that worgen have reached Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine's southeastern hills. Their feral sorcery spread from Shadowfang Keep, where Archmage Arugal unleashed dark enchantments across the forest. Ore from the mine is needed to arm the Undercity. But worgen now make their lair in its shafts, and the mine lies unusable. Grimson the Pale leads the worgen through the mine's infested shafts. Dalar Dawnweaver orders you to slay the corrupted foreman and bring his head to the Sepulcher. With Grimson gone, the worgen will lose their leader, and Forsaken laborers can claim the mine for Lord Varimathras.

quest:425.text: Ivar the Foul. At the Ivar Patch in northern Silverpine, Rane is guarding her badly mauled brother while Ivar the Foul prowls nearby. She asks Horde travelers to kill the savage ghoul so Quinn can recover and they can finish their report to High Executor Hadrec. In northern Silverpine Forest, Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick were sent to survey the forest for High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their work ended in violence at a farmstead, where Ivar the Foul ambushed them. Rane and Quinn escaped, but Quinn was badly mauled. An alchemical remedy made from forest beasts has helped, though he is still too weak to travel. Ivar prowls the nearby barn, waiting for Rane's guard to fail. She asks Horde travelers to enter and kill him, so the homestead can be secured.

quest:428.text: Lost Deathstalkers. In northern Silverpine, two Forsaken scouts have been missing for weeks. High Executor Hadrec sent Rane and Quinn Yorick to watch the abandoned farms, and now you seek word of them. At the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec has heard nothing from Rane and Quinn Yorick for weeks. He sent the pair into northern Silverpine Forest to watch the abandoned farms and track enemy movements. Deathstalkers are the Forsaken’s hidden scouts and killers. They serve Lady Sylvanas, and Hadrec fears the Scourge or another threat has cut them down. Northern Silverpine lies between Lordaeron’s ruined estates and the shadowed borders of Tirisfal Glades. Undead roam there, beasts prowl, and feral worgen make travel perilous even for seasoned rogues. Search the decaying farmsteads where Rane and Quinn Yorick began their survey. Any intelligence they gathered may be vital, if danger has not overtaken them first.

quest:429.text: Wild Hearts. In Silverpine, Rane Yorick seeks help while her brother Quinn lies badly wounded. She needs discolored worg hearts for Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher, whose alchemy may help Quinn recover. Rane Yorick stays beside her brother Quinn, badly wounded after the Deathstalkers' disastrous mission left them pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul mauled him, and he is failing to recover. Ordinary rest cannot mend an undead body torn by such savagery. So Rane turns to the Royal Apothecary Society and its grim arts for a way to put her brother back together. Silverpine's worgs carry the corruption spreading through northern Lordaeron. Their hearts are discolored and hold potent essences. The Royal Apothecaries can distill these blighted organs into concoctions that restore withered Forsaken flesh.

quest:430.text: Return to Quinn. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick waits for a draught that may let him travel again. Apothecary Renferrel sends you from the Sepulcher with the mixture, while Quinn remains wounded in dangerous country. After you gather wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel brews a restorative draught for Quinn Yorick at the Sepulcher. He hands it to you, then returns to his secret alchemical research. You carry the mixture back into the wilderness. At the ruined Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick shelters beside his sister, Deathstalker Rane Yorick. The ghoul Ivar the Foul wounded him so badly he cannot cross hostile ground. Quinn drinks the draught as soon as you arrive. It restores enough strength for him to travel in time, though danger still surrounds the farmstead and Ivar lurks nearby.

quest:433.text: The Public Servant. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Senator Mehr Stonehallow calls for aid against troggs that have halted mining in Dun Morogh. He wants the Rockjaw Bonesnappers driven out so miners can return to work. Mehr Stonehallow serves in Ironforge's Senate and belongs to the Explorers' League. He has come to Gol'Bolar Quarry to direct the response himself. There, he hires travelers and mercenaries to drive the invaders from the mine. Deep digging at Gol'Bolar Quarry broke into sealed hollows underground. Rockjaw troggs poured into the pits, smashed mining equipment, and drove out the workers. Stonehallow wants the Rockjaw Bonesnappers cleared away so Mountaineers can secure the quarry and mining can resume.

quest:435.text: Escorting Erland. In Silverpine, Deathstalker Erland is trying to reach his partner, Rane Yorick. Wolves have trapped him in a shelter, and the way to Rane crosses their hunting ground. Deathstalker Erland is trapped in a shelter by hungry wolves. Even a seasoned Forsaken scout can be overcome by Silverpine's wilds. Wolves circle the ruined refuge, drawn to the little flesh left on Erland's withered frame. Alone, he cannot break through their pack. Deathstalker Erland needs to reach his partner, Rane Yorick, near the Ivar Patch. Wolves prowl the ground between them. Once you guide Erland past the pack, he runs the last stretch to Rane Yorick's outpost. There, the scouts can bring their intelligence together for the Undercity.

quest:436.text: Ironband's Excavation. Jern Hornhelm has sent you from Thelsamar to find out why Ironband's Excavation is making so little progress. Supplies reach Prospector Ironband's team, and Jern trusts his diligence, but the work remains slow. Jern Hornhelm watches from Thelsamar as provisions and tools cross Loch Modan to the Explorers' League. They arrive steadily, yet the dig makes little progress. Jern suspects something is disrupting the work. He needs you to find out what is holding the team back.

quest:437.text: The Dead Fields. In northern Silverpine, Forsaken forces face a Scourge threat at the Dead Fields. High Executor Hadrec sends champions from the Sepulcher against the Rot Hide gnolls and the banshee who shields them. North of the Sepulcher, Rot Hide gnolls overrun an abandoned farmstead. Ordinary farms once stood in these fields. Now plague-ridden scavengers infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec sent small raiding parties to drive them out, but each attack stalled against a strange magical resistance. Nightlash, a Scourge banshee, directs the Rot Hide gnolls.
