When the gnolls face defeat, she scatters Forsaken skirmishers with dark sorcery. Hadrec sends Horde champions to cut down the gnolls and draw Nightlash into the open. He asks for her spectral essence as proof of her destruction.

quest:438.text: The Decrepit Ferry. At the Decrepit Ferry, the Scourge gathers along Lordamere Lake’s shore. High Executor Hadrec sends Forsaken champions east to learn what draws them there. After the Scourge presence in the Dead Fields is suppressed, High Executor Hadrec turns his attention east. The Decrepit Ferry lies among Silverpine Forest’s eastern waterways, where mainland Lordaeron once connected to the island estates of Lordamere Lake. Now undead gather around its rotted piers. Hadrec sends scouts to discover what draws the Lich King’s servants there.

quest:439.text: Rot Hide Clues. At Lordamere Lake, Rot Hide Clues come to light with an engraved ring on a recently deceased woman's hand. When you report the grim find to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher, he sees that Rot Hide gnolls are taking bodies from Tirisfal's mass graves and carrying them to Fenris Isle. Forsaken scouts find a ferry laden with corpses on the shore of Lordamere Lake. Among the dead is the unwrapped, plague-marked hand of a recently slain woman. A plain band on it bears the words “For Deliah.” The ferry points to an organized effort to move the dead, not scavengers feeding at random.

quest:440.text: The Engraved Ring. High Executor Hadrec sends you across the border to Brill with a ring bearing Deliah's name. Magistrate Sevren searches the town records to learn who she was and where the ring came from. Scouts searching for the Rot Hide gnolls in northern Silverpine Forest found Deliah's ring. Magistrate Sevren keeps Tirisfal's civic records and burial registers, though Hadrec doubts any Forsaken still cares for such keepsakes.

quest:441.text: Raleigh and the Undercity. In Brill and the Undercity, a ring draws Raleigh into an old tragedy. Magistrate Sevren sends you to return Deliah's ring to her widowed husband, found after her stolen corpse was bound for Fenris Isle. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren has pieced together clues about a stolen corpse and an engraved ring. The ring belonged to Deliah, and Sevren hopes to learn where it came from and return it to her family. He sends you into the Undercity to find Raleigh, Deliah's surviving husband.

quest:443.text: Rot Hide Ichor. In Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec seeks Rot Hide Ichor before the Forsaken attack Fenris Isle. He wants the fluid studied to understand the gnolls infesting the island. Rot Hide gnolls on Fenris Isle decay and fight with a fury unlike ordinary wild humanoids. They hold strategic ground across Lordamere Lake. High Executor Hadrec believes the strange fluid in their veins may explain their unnatural resilience. He needs samples before the Forsaken commit soldiers to a costly assault. The Royal Apothecary Society works from the Sepulcher, where Apothecary Renferrel studies biological and chemical anomalies. Bring him samples of the putrid fluid. The Forsaken hope to learn where the gnolls came from, who is engineering them, and what weaknesses they have in battle.

quest:444.text: Rot Hide Origins. In Silverpine Forest, the Rot Hides carry a magic Renferrel cannot explain by alchemy alone. He sends a sample to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, where arcane knowledge may reveal its origin. Apothecary Renferrel has reduced fluid from the Rot Hides of Silverpine Forest to its basic elements. His first tests show the ichor bears both necromancy and warlock magic. Alchemy cannot explain the sorcery behind it, so he prepares a sample for an expert in the Undercity.

quest:446.text: Thule Ravenclaw. At the Undercity, a courier brings Bethor Iceshard strange Rot Hide ichor. Bethor recognizes the work of Thule Ravenclaw, his traitorous former colleague, and prepares counter-incantations to help the Forsaken resist the gnolls. Bethor Iceshard studies the courier’s sample in the Undercity’s Magic Quarter and finds an arcane mark. Thule Ravenclaw made the distillation. Before the Third War, Thule was a bright young mage and Bethor’s colleague. When the Lich King rose to power, Thule betrayed his peers and swore himself to the Scourge. As Lordaeron fell, he abandoned his humanity.

quest:447.text:
A Recipe For Death. In Silverpine, A Recipe For Death gathers reagents for the Forsaken's New Plague. From the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel sends bear hearts and spider blood to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. In Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel sees two foes closing on Sylvanas's people. Arthas's legions press them, while remnants of humanity remain enemies. The Forsaken have little hope in conventional warfare. They seek a New Plague that can rot living humans and undead Scourge alike.

Renferrel's field research found a virulent foundation for the plague. Arachnid venom from the Skittering Dark, joined with toxins in the hearts of native bears, forms that base. Bear hearts and spider blood gathered in Silverpine's wilderness travel beneath Lordaeron's ruins to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell oversees the Royal Apothecary Society's design.

Faranell takes Renferrel's samples to test their contaminable properties and refine formulas. The work may secure Forsaken supremacy across the continent.

quest:448.text: Report to Hadrec. In Silverpine, Renferrel sends you to Hadrec as the Scourge threat grows. Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard have investigated the Scourge presence in Lake Lordamere, and High Executor Hadrec now directs preparations against Fenris Isle. Apothecary Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard have studied the danger posed by Thule Ravenclaw, a renegade necromancer. Yet study alone cannot break the Scourge stronghold rising on Fenris Isle. Ravenclaw binds the restless dead there, and Renferrel sees that alchemy and magic will not be enough. The Forsaken military must bring its steel and discipline to bear, so Renferrel sends you to its commander. High Executor Hadrec directs Silverpine Forest's strategic operations for the Dark Lady from the Sepulcher's crypts. Bethor's warnings about Ravenclaw reach him, and Hadrec knows a necromancer entrenched on Lordamere's western shore threatens Undercity's flank. He opens the local garrison's armory to equip the vanguard before sending them against the island fortress.

quest:449.text:
The Deathstalkers' Report. Near the northern wilds, the Deathstalkers have found Scourge forces where the Forsaken did not expect them. You carry their report from the wounded scouts to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher, bringing word that Silverpine Forest holds a greater threat than command believed. The Deathstalkers scout ahead for the Dark Lady, slipping into wild country before the main forces. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, one patrol met fierce resistance while tracking enemy movements.

Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his wounds, while Erland fought his way to safety. Their patrol still gathered intelligence the Forsaken need to hold Silverpine Forest. High Executor Hadrec reads the sealed report and learns that the Scourge hold a stronger presence in Silverpine than Undercity strategists expected. Their forces are more active and aggressive than command believed.

The Forsaken had planned to secure abandoned human hamlets and drive off rogue beasts. Now the Sepulcher's command must prepare for organized Scourge opposition as it fights to claim the region.

quest:450.text: A Recipe For Death. From the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell sends you to Pyrewood Village in A Recipe For Death. You seek Apothecary Berard's notes on the ancient blight that wiped out Lake Lordamere's aquatic life. Apothecary Berard once stood among the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising researchers. He worked in Pyrewood Village, studying past ecological disasters for the Forsaken's alchemical pursuits. Then Archmage Arugal unleashed shadow magic across Silverpine Forest, and Berard fell under its curse. His mind gave way, binding him as a servant to the mage.

quest:451.text: A Recipe For Death. Across Lake Lordamere, Apothecary Renferrel sends you to gather rare reagents for the Royal Apothecary Society. Berard's journal describes mosses and a strange tumor, bound for Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity and his work on a New Plague. Apothecary Berard's death under Arugal's curse cost the Royal Apothecary Society a skilled researcher. His field journal survived, preserving what he learned about blighted life in Silverpine Forest and Lake Lordamere. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel studied the recovered notes and found Berard's account of promising properties in local freshwater organisms. Now Renferrel asks you to carry forward the work his colleague began. Berard's reagents lie among the Dawning Isles, mist-shrouded islands in the eastern waters of Lake Lordamere. Lake skulkers and lake creepers on the isles carry peculiar moss strains that live in tainted water. Berard also noted a hardened tumor among the fierce Vile Fin murloc tribes that nest along the islets and the lake's southern shoreline near Ambermill.

quest:4512.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle seeks ooze samples from Felwood for his studies. He hopes to learn why the Royal Apothecary Society gathers them and what interests the Undercity's alchemists. Laris Geardawdle studies oozes with the Explorers' League. Most of its scholars seek titan relics or dwarven genealogies, but these living puddles resist ordinary classification. They appear in wetlands, cursed woods, and damp ruins. Laris has seen Forsaken apothecaries collecting slime across Lordaeron, and wants to know what draws them to it. Laris believes oozes may be primordial secretions tied to Azeroth's creation. He thinks they are neither vermin nor magical byproducts. To test his theory, you travel across the ocean to Felwood's blighted canopy. There, you gather Cursed and Tainted Oozes in specially made jars. For Laris and many displaced gnomes, these studies carry personal weight. Since Gnomeregan fell to troggs and radiation, thousands have taken refuge in Ironforge's Great Forge. A discovery for the Explorers' League could answer dwarven skeptics. It could show that welcoming gnomes into the mountain city has become an enduring asset to Alliance science.

quest:4513.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. Laris Geardawdle seeks pure oozes across Kalimdor. His Felwood-tainted samples showed that oozes absorb and reflect their surroundings. Clean specimens may show him how they adapt to the places they inhabit. Laris Geardawdle needs clean samples for his study. The tainted ones showed how oozes take on the traits of their surroundings, but left him without a clear comparison. He seeks samples untouched by demonic taint or urban filth, so he can study ooze life on its own.

quest:452.text: Pyrewood Ambush. In Pyrewood Village, Deathstalker Faerleia waits while Arugal's council keeps the afflicted in line. The Forsaken aim to break his hold on the town and weaken his position in Shadowfang Keep. Deathstalker Faerleia waits in Pyrewood Village's town hall for the local leaders. Archmage Arugal tends his dark sorceries in Shadowfang Keep, leaving the Pyrewood Council to keep order among the afflicted villagers. Faerleia plans to ambush the council. Without its mediation, the Forsaken hope the worgen in the woods and village streets will break free of Arugal's control.

quest:454.text: After the Ambush. Miran needs an escort to carry blasting powder to Loch Modan’s southern excavation site. Dark Iron dwarves ambushed the supply run, and the road is still dangerous. Saean and his conspirators attacked the supply run. Barrels were scattered, and the road became perilous. Huldar remains behind to guard the powder left there. Miran prepares to move ahead with the next load, so the supply line is split. The southern excavation site needs blasting powder to break stone and uncover titan relics. Miran fears another ambush from the ridges. He seeks a companion before loading his cargo and setting out past any traps the Dark Irons may have prepared.

quest:460.text: Resting in Pieces. On Fenris Isle, Alaric's severed head calls for help from beyond the grave. He asks you to carry it across Fenris Keep to an unmarked grave near the stables, where his body lies. At Fenris Keep in Silverpine Forest, Alaric served Thule Ravenclaw as chief servant and personal bodyguard. Thule was a powerful mage aligned with the Scourge. When the Plague of Undeath swept through the region, he promised his sorcery would shield Alaric. Instead, the ward trapped him in endless agony and undeath, while his awareness remained in his severed parts. Thule made the rot hide gnolls by infecting local packs with necromantic decay. Then he turned on his own bodyguard. He cut off Alaric's head and threw it to the savage gnolls as a diversion. The rot hides dragged Alaric's body to a shallow grave they had hastily dug outside the keep's stables. They kept his speaking head as a grim plaything until an outsider intervened.

quest:461.text: The Hidden Niche. In Fenris Keep, Alaric's memories guide you toward a hidden alcove. His remains point to a place of rest, and an old relic waits there. Alaric remembers Fenris Keep in its better days. Horde scouts lifted his bones from a shallow grave outside the stronghold, but he will not go quietly to the Sepulcher. He offers vital knowledge in return: a hidden niche in the keep's southwestern tower holds an item treasured by Thule Ravenclaw and his fellow mages.

quest:4681.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore's coast, dead sea creatures have drawn Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde into a troubling inquiry. She serves the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and seeks the cause of the strandings and deaths. Dead sea creatures line Darkshore's beaches and shallows, leaving the night elves of Auberdine puzzled. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde has already examined one stranded creature on the beach. Now she asks you to dive west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, and inspect the bones of a massive sea turtle. Those remains will help her report to the Temple of the Moon.

quest:4722.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore, a Beached Sea Turtle lies among the surf as murlocs scavenge its remains. Auberdine naturalists seek sound samples to send to Darnassus for study. Dead sea turtles drift ashore along Darkshore’s coast, or beach themselves in confusion. Their remains soon draw scavengers. Greymist murlocs have made crude camps around this turtle’s skeletal frame and carve away its flesh and shell. Yet bone, shell, or tissue may remain intact in the wreckage. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde works in Auberdine as a field researcher, recording unusual marine life and disturbances along the coast. Night elves regard stranded beasts with reverence and scientific curiosity. Suitable remains are cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus. They seek to learn why so many giants of the open sea wash ashore.

quest:4723.text: Beached Sea Creature. At Mist's Edge, a giant sea thresher lies stranded as murlocs feed on its carcass. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for night elf researchers in Darnassus, who seek to learn why deep-sea giants wash ashore. Along Mist's Edge, enormous thresher remains have joined the shipwrecks and debris washed in by the tide. The beast dwarfs the wildlife of Darkshore's shallows. Its size suggests it came from beyond the Veiled Sea, from waters far from the calm waters here. Murlocs swarm over the corpse, but they lack the strength and coordination to bring down such a creature. Something else killed the predator before the sea carried it ashore. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde coordinates the salvage of bones and biological samples from Darkshore's stranded sea giants. Night elf researchers in Darnassus hope the remains will show whether illness, disturbances in the deep sea, or arcane corruption drives the giants onto the killing sands.

quest:4725.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's shore, a broken carriage rests on the shell of a Beached Sea Turtle. Greymist murlocs gather around the great carcass. You find a broken carriage strapped across a giant sea turtle's shell on Darkshore's misty shore. Many sea creatures have washed up along this coast, but this turtle carried a load. Its handlers drove it onto the beach. Now the carriage lies abandoned in the tide. Greymist murlocs swarm the turtle's remains. They have made a den among the rotting meat and scavenged timber. A marked container lies among their refuse and the broken carriage frame. The turtle's former masters left it there.

quest:4727.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s northern shore, a Beached Sea Turtle lies untouched by nearby Greymist murlocs. A sample goes to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to learn why great sea creatures wash ashore and scavengers leave them alone. Greymist murlocs crowd Darkshore’s northern coast and scavenge food washed up from the Veiled Sea. Yet the great turtle’s bones lie mostly untouched. Those who study the shore wonder whether the murlocs missed it or avoid it for some unknown reason. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples from beached sea turtles for the Temple of the Moon. The night elf priestesses study disturbances in Darkshore’s waters. Skeletal fragments may help them learn whether sickness, magic, or dangerous sea predators are killing the ancient creatures.

quest:4728.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a giant sea mammal lies washed ashore beside an abandoned dig site. Its carcass and scattered tools draw murlocs and travelers. On Darkshore's sand lies a giant sea mammal, partly gutted and worn by the sea. A rusted wheelbarrow and discarded tools mark where an orderly study began. The researchers left before they could finish. Dwarven field researchers from the Explorer's League were studying the carcass in Darkshore. Their work stopped when local murlocs swarmed the site to scavenge. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde acts for the Temple of the Moon. She accepts salvaged bone samples to help study the unnatural wash-ups along the coast.

quest:4730.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a great sea mammal lies half-devoured on the sand. Murlocs gather around it, and Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples to learn why gentle sea beasts are dying on the shore. Far north along Darkshore's lonely beaches, a great sea mammal lies rotting and half-eaten. Murlocs pick over its bones, more vicious than usual. These beasts were gentle in life, and their deaths trouble the coast as much as the blighted forests inland. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde says these gentle mammals live in the waters around Teldrassil's base. Unlike aggressive threshers, they have never been known to drive themselves onto the rocks. The Temple of the Moon is gathering bone samples to learn what corruption or threat drives them from the deep.

quest:4731.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's coast, a Beached Sea Turtle lies dead beneath the carriage it once hauled. A box marked with strange runes rests in the wreckage. A dead sea turtle lies among the ancient bones along Darkshore's coast. Splintered carriage boards cling to its broad shell. It was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo, not stranded by sickness or confusion. A container carved with unfamiliar, serpent-like marks lies in the wreckage, where scavengers feed on the remains.

quest:4732.text:
Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore, Beached Sea Turtle remains wash ashore in growing numbers. Their bones give Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine specimens to study as Kalimdor's marine life dwindles. Great sea creatures and turtles lie along Darkshore's shore. Many ancient turtles drift onto the shoals or crawl onto the sand to die. Greymist murlocs gather at the carcasses and strip away the flesh. Soon, only shell and bone remain, beside crude camps they make there. Before the Third War, sea turtles thrived in the sacred waters around Mount Hyjal and the roots of Nordrassil, the World Tree. After Nordrassil's sacrifice against the Burning Legion and Teldrassil's planting off Kalimdor's northern shore, their numbers collapsed.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde and other priestesses of Elune study the remains for the Temple of the Moon. They seek to learn whether dark magic, changing seas, or the loss of the turtles' ancient sanctuary drives them to their deaths.

quest:4733.text: Beached Sea Creature. A colossal thresher lies stranded on Darkshore's rocky Twilight Shore. Its death and stranding deepen the sea troubles worrying the night elves. Along the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore, driftwood and sea debris wash into the inlets. In one, you find the remains of an enormous thresher. Tides and scavengers have begun to pick it apart, yet its skeleton dwarfs the ordinary predators in these coastal shallows. The giant does not belong in these waters. Sickness or disorientation may have driven it onto the rocks, or a deeper disturbance may lie in the Veiled Sea.

quest:4740.text: WANTED: Murkdeep!. Auberdine's council wants Murkdeep dead for a Sentinel's death and ships lost off Darkshore. Find the Greymist chieftain south along the coast. Greymist murlocs are usually a nuisance along Darkshore. Murkdeep has turned against Auberdine, and the wanted poster outside the inn names him as the killer of at least one night elf Sentinel. It also suspects him of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels offshore. With ships lost and raids along the coast, the Auberdine Village Council has set a public bounty on their leader. Murkdeep lurks off the southern coast near murloc huts clustered around a bonfire. Trespassers face an organized defense as Greymist coastrunners and shore-crawlers surge from the surf to protect their settlement. Then Murkdeep emerges with his vanguard to strike the intruders. Proof of Murkdeep's death answers the Sentinels' grim need. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea handles the council's bounty payout. With Greymist leadership broken, travelers and ships on Darkshore's foggy coast gain a reprieve from sabotage.

quest:4761.text: Thundris Windweaver. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver hears that the Blackwood furbolgs have grown hostile. Terenthis sends you with news of their growing aggression, and Thundris seeks the cause of the corruption spreading through Darkshore. You bring Terenthis’s report to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine after scouting corrupted furbolg camps in Darkshore. Terenthis stays in the wilds to investigate the spreading corruption. As village elder, Thundris watches over daily life and weighs the spiritual and environmental dangers facing the kaldorei. Your report gives Auberdine’s leaders proof that the furbolgs’ troubles reach beyond territory: an unnatural malice is taking hold of them. Thundris has heard that the forest dwellers near Auberdine have grown hostile. Yet the furbolgs are not his only concern. Corruption spreads through Darkshore’s soil, plants, and waters. Thundris believes the land cannot heal until someone finds the source of the blight. So he turns to the waterways and calls on capable allies to trace the taint upstream.

quest:4762.text: The Cliffspring River. Foul water now runs down the Cliffspring River toward Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver sends Alliance investigators to collect a sample from the pool beneath a road bridge waterfall. He suspects the corruption began beyond the riverbanks. From the eastern highlands, the Cliffspring River runs to the coastal shoals of Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Now its waters carry an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Thundris Windweaver fears the foul water will poison the shores and the town's supplies. So he sends scouts upriver to take samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

quest:4763.text: The Blackwood Corrupted. In northern Darkshore, the Blackwood Corrupted are caught in a dark influence. Evidence in the tainted waters of Cliffspring River leads Thundris Windweaver to send you against it. You gather their food and purify it with moonwell water, drawing the demonic handler into the open and breaking his hold on the northern camp. In Auberdine, the night elves have long wondered why the once-peaceful Blackwood furbolgs turned on their neighbors. Their search along Cliffspring River traced the rot to satyr meddling. These ancient servants of the Burning Legion manipulate the tribe with fel magic. Insidious talismans twist the furbolgs' minds and drive them into feral aggression.

quest:477.text: Border Crossings. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends you after Dalaran's supplies and the reason the Kirin Tor support Ambermill. Their crates pass through Silverpine Forest on the way to a Dalaran camp near Pyrewood Village. Wagons bring Dalaran's supplies and arcane goods from the Hillsbrad Foothills through Silverpine Forest. They serve the outposts and staging grounds along the way. Just north of Pyrewood Village, a camp holds Dalaran personnel who watch the road. Ambermill is the main human stronghold still standing in eastern Silverpine, and Dalaran continues to support it. Shadow Priest Allister and the Forsaken leaders at the Sepulcher want to know why Dalaran gives Ambermill so much support. They suspect the Kirin Tor would not risk lives and supplies deep in Forsaken territory for a provincial town alone. Some greater strategic or magical purpose may be behind it. Intercepting the crates could show the Forsaken what Dalaran is sending west.

quest:478.text: Maps and Runes. In Silverpine, maps and runes reveal Dalaran's interest in Ambermill. Horde agents recover a hidden crate for Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher. Horde agents find a Dalaran crate hidden along the border routes near Ambermill. Detailed regional charts and a rune-inscribed pendant lie inside. Human sentries stand nearby, so the scouts retrieve the artifact carefully. Dalaran's arcane reach lies close to their borders.

quest:479.text: Ambermill Investigations. At Ambermill, Dalaran wizards weave magic that threatens the Forsaken’s hold on Silverpine Forest. From the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends agents to disrupt their work and seize the magical foci. Ambermill lies in the eastern hills of Silverpine Forest. Its human residents are wizards and defenders pledged to the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. The mages weave powerful magic in a vast ritual. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister and his companion Dalar see the danger. If the Kirin Tor channel their power unchecked, the Forsaken risk losing Silverpine entirely. As Dalar scries the forest and traces the magic, Allister sends agents against the practitioners in Ambermill. Dalaran conjurers, mages, and their protectors wear enchanted pendants that focus and coordinate their arts. Take the talismans from slain sorcerers, and the ritual falters. This buys the Sepulcher time to find the ringleader directing the arcane weave.

quest:481.text: Dalar's Analysis. In Silverpine, Allister's report sends a Dalaran relic to Dalar for study. A rune-inscribed pendant taken from a supply crate reaches Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. The relic shows that Dalaran's surviving mages are gathering great magical power for a hidden purpose. A supply crate from Dalaran is raided at a camp north of Pyrewood Village. Beneath old maps, Shadow Priest Allister finds a rune-inscribed pendant. Its enchantment is beyond his spiritual knowledge, so he sends it to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. Dalar's skill as an arcane scholar makes him better suited to read Dalaran's magical warding.

quest:4811.text: The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea asks you to investigate a red crystal in Darkshore's eastern mountains. Moonkin are multiplying nearby and seem drawn to it, and the Sentinels need to know whether the crystal is real. Moonkin were once gentle, mystical creatures bound to Kalimdor's wilds. Now aggressive packs multiply along the slopes east of Auberdine. Some night elves still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea puts the town's safety first as danger grows. Reports point to a single spot among the eastern peaks. Scouts and wanderers speak of an unnatural red crystal jutting from a rocky hillside high above Darkshore. Rumors travel easily along the fogbound coast, so Glynda wants you to see the place for yourself. The crystal is real. The Sentinels still need to learn why moonkin gather there and whether it threatens the land.

quest:4812.text: As Water Cascades. At Auberdine, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea hopes moonwell water will reveal what lies beneath Darkshore's red crystal. Sacred water may pierce its opaque surface. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea seeks a safe way to study the red crystal high on Darkshore's eastern cliffs. Moonwell water bears divine, restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda believes water from Auberdine's moonwell may react with the strange stone and pierce its opaque shell without destroying it.

quest:4813.text: The Fragments Within. At the eastern cliffs, you return to the red crystal with water from a moonwell. It may reveal what lies within, and you carry the finding back to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine. Back in Auberdine, you tell Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea what you found. The discovery gives the local night elf leaders more cause for concern, but no clear answers. Glynda will present the findings to the town council. The crystal rests high on the eastern cliffs, far enough from town to bring her some comfort; it poses no immediate danger.

quest:482.text:
Dalaran's Intentions. In Silverpine Forest, Dalar Dawnweaver sends Shadow Priest Allister a warning. A pendant bound for the Kirin Tor in Ambermill reveals their plan to awaken a dormant ley energy node beneath the town. At the Sepulcher, the Forsaken prepare to answer. Dalar Dawnweaver studies a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate. It recalls an old Kirin Tor survey of Ambermill. The quiet village was chosen for a reason: it sits atop a dormant ley energy node. Dalar realizes the wizards intend to tap its power.

Awakening such a nexus takes immense magical reserves. The enchanted pendants the wizards wear are key to channeling and catalyzing that power. The Forsaken cannot abide a fortified Kirin Tor outpost fueled by ley energy. It would threaten the southern approaches to the Sepulcher and Tirisfal Glades. Whatever ritual the magi prepare, raw ley energy would give Dalaran an enormous strategic advantage in Lordaeron.

So Dalar urgently sends word to Shadow Priest Allister. He asks Allister to devise a way to stall the wizards before their ritual is complete.

quest:486.text: Ursal the Mauler. In Teldrassil, Athridas Bearmantle seeks to rouse the Druids of the Talon from an unnatural sleep. Their kin are trapped in the Barrow Den, and Ursal the Mauler's corruption must be broken. The Druids of the Talon went to the Barrow Den of Ban'ethil to sleep and commune with the Emerald Dream. Their peaceful trance became a prison, with no path back to waking. Athridas Bearmantle traced the trouble to the gnarlpine furbolgs and their vicious leader, Ursal the Mauler. Ursal meddled with the druids' sacred rite, leaving them caught between waking and the Dream. The Relics of Wakening alone cannot carry Athridas through the spiritual fog to the druids. The source of the interference must end. Ursal the Mauler lairs in Gnarlpine Hold, home to the tribe in far southwestern Teldrassil. Slaying the furbolg warlord breaks his hold on the sleepers' minds.

quest:491.text:
Wand to Bethor. At Fenris Keep, the Woven Wand is bound for Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Three apprentice mages made it as a sign of fellowship, but Thule Ravenclaw hid it after choosing the Scourge. Its return brings a piece of Bethor's mortal youth back to the Magic Quarter. Before Lordaeron fell, three young mages joined their training wands into one: the Woven Wand. It marked their friendship and their shared hopes in the magical arts.

Then Thule Ravenclaw gave his loyalty to the Lich King and embraced the Scourge. Their fellowship was broken. He came to despise the friendship they had shared, yet could neither destroy the wand nor leave it with his former companions.

quest:492.text: A New Plague. In Brill, A New Plague faces its first test on a captive dwarf. Apothecary Johaan sends you to the cellar of Gallows' End Tavern with the brew he made from reagents gathered across Tirisfal Glades. Apothecary Johaan has brought his research to a dangerous trial. The Royal Apothecary Society serves Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, seeking a plague that kills the living while leaving undead bodies unharmed. Johaan has brewed what he calls a “special drink.” He sends you to give it to an imprisoned enemy of the Forsaken. In Brill, the Deathguard keeps captives in a damp cellar beneath Gallows' End Tavern. They await interrogation or disposal. One prisoner is a Dwarven Mountaineer, an Ironforge scout caught trespassing in Tirisfal Glades. Defiant and thirsty, he eagerly accepts the drink, unaware of what Johaan mixed into it.

quest:5041.text: Supplies for the Crossroads. Thork needs supplies back at the Crossroads after Razormane quilboar raids. The stolen crates carry provisions the outpost needs as conflict spreads across the Barrens. Thork needs provisions returned to the Crossroads after a supply caravan is ambushed. The outpost links Horde travel, trade, and defense across the Barrens. Its cargo comes from Durotar and Mulgore. Without those goods, shortages of provisions, tools, and arms threaten daily life in the harsh wilderness. Razormane quilboar have taken the crates. These swine-beasts contest Horde control across central Kalimdor. They hauled the cargo to their thorn-bush camps and keep it there. Thork sends trusted warriors into Razormane territory to recover supplies for the Horde.

quest:5061.text: Aquatic Form. You bring the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion back to Darnassus. The rite teaches Alliance druids to attune their spirits to deep waters. For Cenarion Circle initiates, shapeshifting binds a druid’s spirit to the wild aspects of Azeroth. Young night elf druids endure trials in the dark coastal depths and in Moonglade. There, Dendrite Starblaze gives them the assembled Pendant of the Sea Lion. They carry this sacred token back to Teldrassil, proof of their respect for the laws of air, water, and breath. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits your return in the Cenarion Enclave. Your trials along the coasts of Darkshore and Westfall have tested your endurance and attunement. Present the completed pendant to show Bearwalker that your mind and body are ready to shed their mortal skin. Then you can take the swift, breathing form of the sea lion.

quest:543.text: The Perenolde Tiara. Count Remington Ridgewell sends mercenaries into the Ruins of Alterac for a lost heirloom. The Perenolde Tiara once adorned Alterac's royal family and now rests with an ogre mage. Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara made by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. Alterac was conquered and collapsed. When Alterac City fell, many royal treasures vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage among the Crushridge ogres, holds the tiara in the ruins. He searches the broken stones for baubles and abandoned wealth. Count Remington Ridgewell, a collector of historical oddities in Stormwind City, learns the tiara survived. He hires mercenaries to enter ogre-held territory, defeat Grel'borg, and return the jewel to his gallery.

quest:5502.text: A Warden of the Horde. In Orgrimmar, Grunth returns to Orphan Matron Battlewail as Children's Week ends. After seeing the world with you, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself. After your travels together, Grunth thanks you for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. He recalls his parents' advice to rise above hardship and hopes to become a hero like you. Now he asks to return home and tell the matron about your time together. You bring Grunth back to Orphan Matron Battlewail at the orphanage in the Valley of Honor. In the new Horde, caring for the young is a solemn duty, for war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail praises your compassion as the true measure of a Horde hero. Grunth gives you a beloved pet so you will remember the bond formed on your travels.

quest:5713.text: One Shot. One Kill.. On the road to Auberdine, Sentinel Aynasha is ambushed and cannot carry her message onward. Poisoned by Marosh the Devious and his furbolg trackers, she must mix an antidote before she can travel. Sentinel Aynasha carries important communications toward Auberdine when hostile furbolgs intercept her on a trail in northern Kalimdor. Marosh the Devious leads them. Their venom leaves the scout unsteady and unable to continue on foot. Aynasha knows how to make natural remedies, but the antidote takes time to mix and take effect. Marosh's trackers are closing in, so she needs travelers to guard her as she works. Though her strength is failing, she keeps her bow steady and fires into the brush to hold the attackers back.

quest:5722.text: Searching for the Lost Satchel. Rahauro sends you from Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise into Ragefire Chasm, where Magatha Grimtotem awaits news of her missing emissary Maur. Magatha Grimtotem learns on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise that her emissary, Maur Grimtotem, entered the cavern beneath Orgrimmar. He meant to study the troggs and try to parley with them, but never returned. Rumors say he found something unusual shortly before his death. While Warchief Thrall and his advisers attend to the Shadow Council in Ragefire Chasm, the Grimtotem clan pursues its own interests.

quest:5723.text: Testing an Enemy's Strength. At Thunder Bluff, Rahauro answers the slaughter of Magatha Grimtotem's emissaries beneath Orgrimmar. He sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to thin the troggs' ranks. Magatha Grimtotem sent tauren emissaries into the fiery depths beneath Orgrimmar to make peace with the troggs. The creatures slaughtered the delegates on arrival. Magatha took the massacre as an insult to the tauren and a growing danger to the Horde. So she resolved to answer with force. From Thunder Bluff, Rahauro carries out Magatha’s orders. He sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to find and kill trogg warriors and shamans. The Horde strikes deep into their underground home, thinning their numbers before they can pour through the tunnels into Orgrimmar.

quest:5724.text: Returning the Lost Satchel. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, you find Maur Grimtotem's satchel and carry it to Rahauro on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Troggs slew Maur Grimtotem in the fiery depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Even in death, his arms held fast to his personal satchel. Freeing it from his grasp gives you the only clue to why a member of the Grimtotem clan entered the volcanic caverns beneath Thrall's capital.

quest:5725.text: The Power to Destroy.... From the Undercity, Varimathras sends Horde adventurers beneath Orgrimmar. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner seeks two dark tomes from the Searing Blade cult, hoping their power will aid her war against the Scourge and the Lich King. Thrall's orcs hunt the Searing Blade cult beneath their capital. The Forsaken covet the cult's occult stores. On Sylvanas Windrunner's orders, Varimathras sends operatives into Ragefire Chasm to seize two demonic grimoires: Spells of Shadow and Incantations from the Nether. The Dark Lady believes disciplined Forsaken will can use these gifts better than the lesser cultists. Once the tomes are secured, Varimathras explains their purpose. Their dark magic is meant to strengthen Sylvanas's campaign against the Scourge. The Forsaken hope to claim every scrap of forbidden power, break the Lich King's hold across Lordaeron, and free the remaining undead from his mental enslavement.

quest:5726.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall begins a covert search for the Burning Blade in Durotar. He asks a promising young adventurer to recover a Lieutenant's Insignia from Skull Rock, opening a way to uncover cultists working under the Horde's nose. In Durotar, the new Horde struggles to secure a home, and Warchief Thrall faces betrayal from within. The Burning Blade has taken root just outside Orgrimmar's gates. Its cultists prey on lingering demonic corruption and hunger for dark power. Thrall needs someone to watch and listen without drawing notice. Skull Rock lies east of Orgrimmar. Its rugged caverns hold warlocks, voidwalkers, and fanatical cultists. Thrall sends you to take a Lieutenant's Insignia from one of the Burning Blade leaders. The emblem is meant to open the cult's hidden ranks, so Thrall can learn who directs its movements.

quest:5727.text: Hidden Enemies. In Orgrimmar, Thrall sends you to learn what the Burning Blade knows. Cult activity at Skull Rock has brought you to Neeru Fireblade with a lieutenant's insignia, to test his loyalties. Thrall chooses cunning over a strike at the Cleft of Shadow. He knows Neeru Fireblade pretends to serve the Horde while secretly aiding the cultists. A direct attack could warn Neeru's masters and end the trail into the conspiracy. So Thrall gives you an insignia taken from the cult in Durotar and asks you to pose as an initiate, learning what Neeru knows.

quest:5728.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you against the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. You have won Neeru Fireblade's trust by pretending to share the cult's cause. Now Thrall sends you into Ragefire Chasm to strike at its leaders. Orgrimmar was built as a haven for a free Orcish race. Yet beneath its markets, the Cleft of Shadow opens onto the tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. There, remnants of the Shadow Council gather strength as the Searing Blade. They practice dark arts and scheme to seize the young Horde from within its own capital.

quest:5729.text: Hidden Enemies. In Orgrimmar, Thrall's watch reaches into the Cleft of Shadow. After Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker die beneath the city, Thrall sends you to win Neeru Fireblade's trust. Thrall sees a chance after Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed in Ragefire Chasm. He chooses to leave Neeru Fireblade in place. Neeru has lost the lieutenants who led the local cult. So Thrall sends you back to the Cleft of Shadow, offering yourself as an ally who can fill that gap.

quest:5730.text: Hidden Enemies. In Orgrimmar, Thrall awaits your report on the Burning Blade. Neeru Fireblade trusts you, and the Warchief needs to know how far the cult's reach extends across Kalimdor.

quest:5761.text: Slaying the Beast. Neeru Fireblade sends Horde adventurers from Orgrimmar into Ragefire Chasm to hunt Taragaman the Hungerer. He says Warchief Thrall ordered the hunt and asks for the felguard’s heart as proof the demonic cult has fallen. Ragefire Chasm runs beneath Orgrimmar’s red earthen streets. Its fiery fissure shelters troggs, beasts, and covert Searing Blade agents. In the Cleft of Shadow above, Neeru Fireblade claims to serve Thrall and cleanse the demonic rot. He points to Taragaman the Hungerer, a massive felguard in the cavern’s heart, and calls him the mastermind behind the cult beneath the city.

quest:6121.text: Lessons Anew. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends Alliance druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of cleansing poison. There, Dendrite Starblaze begins their instruction in venom and toxins. Cenarius teaches druids and blesses them with a bond to the living world. Among his gifts is the power to cleanse venom with a simple incantation. Such power comes with a burden. Before young druids wield it, they learn the hard, ordinary work of fighting toxins without nature's magic. Mathrengyl Bearwalker trains druids in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus. Now he sends his student beyond local practice to Moonglade. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze coordinates the Cenarion Circle's wider efforts. He has practical work for the novice.

quest:6122.text: The Principal Source. At Cliffspring Falls, sick deer have drawn the Cenarion Circle to the water. Dendrite Starblaze sends young druids from Moonglade to gather a sample for Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore with fresh water. When deer began to suffer a lingering sickness, the Cenarion Circle looked to the river for its cause. Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade suspects the water is tainted. He sends novice druids to gather a sample at the cavern mouth beneath the falls. Vicious naga dwell inside Cliffspring River Cave, near the falls' headwaters. Their presence endangers anyone who comes to study the blight. The Cenarion Circle needs a sample from the cave mouth to learn what is making the wilderness sick.

quest:6123.text: Gathering the Cure. In Darkshore, sick deer need a salve, and Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine shows a young druid how to make one. The remedy calls for water and healing plants gathered nearby. Alanndarian Nightsong seeks a cure for Darkshore's sick deer. A contaminated water source has harmed the local wildlife, so sampled Cliffspring water will form the salve's base. Natural ingredients with healing power must complete the mixture. The deer cannot recover alone, and the Cenarion Circle needs a remedy soon. Earthroot and Lunar Fungus lend healing power to the salve. Earthroot grows in rocky soil, where a practiced herbalist's eye helps find it. Lunar Fungus blooms in caves east of Auberdine. The moonkin there have grown territorial and agitated, making the gathering more dangerous.

quest:6124.text: Curing the Sick. Across Darkshore, deer are falling sick, and Curing the Sick brings you a way to help them. Alanndarian Nightsong gives you salve for the poisoned animals before you report to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Deer are falling sick across Darkshore, from the Cliffspring River south to the border of Ashenvale. They wander the misty woods, weakened by toxins in the soil and streams. After you gather the needed reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong gives you freshly brewed animal salve to treat them.

quest:6125.text: Power over Poison. In Darnassus, Power over Poison brings a young druid back to finish the Cenarion Circle's trial. It began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong sends young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They use them to brew a salve for stricken wildlife. Before teaching the magic that purges toxins, the Cenarion Circle asks initiates to learn the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. That work shows them what common folk endure when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care. The remedy proves effective in Auberdine, and Starblaze sends the druid across the sea to Darnassus. Mathrengyl Bearwalker waits in the Cenarion Enclave. Pleased by the initiate's grace under pressure, he teaches them to cleanse toxins through nature's power. Yet virulent poisons in the wilds around Auberdine trouble him. They point to an unnatural blight that disturbs the land's balance.

quest:6126.text: Lessons Anew. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids to sacred Moonglade to learn the cleansing of poisons. Under Dendrite Starblaze, a night elf druid, apprentices begin that study as real poisonings call for more than practice. Cenarius granted druids an incantation to purge virulent toxins, and charged them to protect the wilds. Turak Runetotem teaches that such magic needs a firm grounding. Before using it to clear a blight, a druid must understand venom’s physical toll and learn to treat it by ordinary means. Turak sends promising acolytes north from Mulgore along sacred pathways to Moonglade. There, in the peaceful village of Nighthaven, ancient night elf mentors such as Dendrite Starblaze teach practitioners of both elf and tauren kind. Their shared study reflects the Cenarion Circle’s delicate truce, rising above the political strife between Horde and Alliance.

quest:6127.text: The Principal Source. From Moonglade, Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a sample of water. She asks them to carry it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it may explain the poison harming wildlife. Dendrite Starblaze fears the Burning Blade has tainted Dreadmist Peak. The mountain rises northwest of the Crossroads, above the dry northern Barrens. Springs and pools crown its heights, shaping the local weather and moisture. Now a cult devoted to demons has taken hold on the crags, and its foul sorcery may poison the basin. Sick gazelles stumble across the northern savanna, north of the main east-west trail through the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem seeks help for the local tauren and asks the Cenarion Circle to learn what is poisoning the herd. A water sample from the peak will let him study the sickness and brew an antidote.

quest:6128.text: Gathering the Cure. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem guides young tauren druids through a sacred passage. You gather earthroot and sturdy kodo horns for a salve to treat the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Tonga Runetotem needs ingredients for an antidote, using the water sample you secured at Dreadmist Peak. Earthroot gives the salve its medicinal qualities, while ground kodo horn lends it the strength to drive venom from a creature's system. For a young druid, gathering these means relying on the earth's gifts and hunting local beasts. As Tonga Runetotem prepares the salve, he teaches the limits of physical medicine. Herbal lore and alchemy can counter certain toxins, but most poisons need their own cure. Rather than carry endless herbs and horns, druids learn to attune to nature's healing energies. That lesson leads to the druidic art of Cure Poison.

quest:6129.text: Curing the Sick. Sick gazelles are suffering across the northern Barrens. Tonga Runetotem sends young Horde druids to treat them with a freshly made herbal salve, then sends them before the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. An unnatural sickness is spreading among gazelles in the northern Barrens. You have gathered earthroot and kodo horns for a curative remedy, and Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads now entrusts the animals to your care. Search north of the main crossroads and tend to ten suffering gazelles. The salve brings them relief before the affliction takes deeper hold in the ecosystem. After you apply the salve, you travel to Moonglade’s tranquil druidic sanctuary. Dendrite Starblaze recognizes your compassion and vigilance there. He says the gazelles’ suffering points to a deeper corruption stalking Kalimdor’s wilderness. By tending even the lowliest beasts, tauren druids show that reverence for Cenarius reaches beyond tribal boundaries. They earn deeper secrets of poison cleansing and nature magic.

quest:6130.text: Power over Poison. At Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to claim the gift of Cure Poison. The initiate has treated poisoned gazelles near the Crossroads with herbal mixtures and now faces Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise. The Cenarion Circle asks a druid to learn how affliction feels before granting the power to cleanse venom. Dendrite Starblaze sends the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem has them gather ingredients for a salve. By treating the Barrens' poisoned gazelles by hand, without spiritual aid, the druid sees how ordinary creatures struggle against natural and unnatural toxins. After the trial, Dendrite sends the initiate to Turak Runetotem, the grand druid trainer on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Turak warns that strange, virulent poisons near the Crossroads threaten the plains' natural balance. He commends the initiate's grace under pressure and grants the spiritual art of curing poisons. The living creatures of Kalimdor are now in the initiate's care.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, The Forgotten Heirloom is a pocket watch left behind as the Furlbrows fled their farm. Recovering it gives them a chance to reclaim something personal amid the chaos. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts from the pumpkin patches woke them in the night, leaving little time to gather what they could carry. In their flight, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. Defias thugs and thieves, including Benny Blaanco, now pick through the abandoned Furlbrow farm. Returning for a keepsake could mean death for ordinary folk. You can take the pocket watch from the wardrobe and restore a measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything to Westfall's lawlessness.

quest:6401.text: Kaya's Alive. Makaba Flathoof has word that Kaya Flathoof survived the Grimtotem attack in Stonetalon. He sends you to Sun Rock Retreat, where her aunt Tammra Windfield waits anxiously. The Grimtotem strike along Stonetalon's contested trails. When their village came under attack, young Kaya Flathoof was feared dead or taken by the renegades. Her rescue brings relief while tribes still fight among the crags. Makaba Flathoof sends you from Kaya to Sun Rock Retreat with news of her safety. Her aunt, Tammra Windfield, waits there anxiously for word from the trails. Your message comforts the family and keeps the remote Horde outpost connected.

quest:6421.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Kobolds dig for Resonite in the Stonetalon Mountains, while Mor'rogal at Sun Rock Retreat fears a growing unrest in the earth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal watches the Stonetalon peaks and feels the earth stir. An unnatural agitation rises from the southeast. In Boulderslide Ravine, kobolds have abandoned their usual foraging and now dig fiercely for Resonite, a rare mineral from beneath the surface. Mor'rogal sends Horde scouts past the kobolds and into the cave's deepest reaches. He asks them to bring back raw samples and learn why the kobolds mine with such frenzy.

quest:6441.text: Satyr Horns. At Splintertree Post, Satyr Horns offer Pixel a chance to trade in Ratchet. The traveling goblin seeks them for the journey south to the port town. At Splintertree Post, Pixel sees a chance to profit while resting between travels. Satyr horns fetch a high price in Ratchet, and Pixel wants them for the journey back south to the port town. Rather than face the corrupted creatures, Pixel hires passing adventurers to bring back sixteen intact horns. Demonic satyrs haunt scattered, fel-tainted ruins across Ashenvale. They are remnants of a betrayal during the ancient sundering. You can search their strongholds at Night Run, the fortified camp of Satyrnaar, and the shadowed groves of Xavian. Pixel seeks horns from any of these places for Ratchet's merchant wharves.

quest:6442.text: Naga at the Zoram Strand. Along Ashenvale's coast, Naga threaten the Horde's hold at Zoram Strand. From Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai seeks to drive the Wrathtail away from the sunken ruins of ancient Zoram. The Horde's hold at Zoram Strand is fragile. The outpost stands amid hostile night elf territory and bitter woodland fighting, yet its coast gives the Horde a link to the sea. Now aggressive naga have crawled ashore. They could cut off that route and overwhelm the small garrison before its defenses are ready. Beneath Zoram Strand's sandy shoals lie the shattered remains of Zoram, an ancient elven city swallowed by the Great Sundering thousands of years ago. Marukai and the outpost's defenders do not know why the Wrathtail have come from the deep trenches now. Their sudden interest in the sunken ruins threatens anyone walking above them. Marukai sees a simple fight for survival. With swords and tridents drawn, reason matters little. She demands twenty severed heads from the Wrathtail. She hopes force will drive the naga back into the depths and secure the shore for the Horde.

quest:6461.text: Blood Feeders. In Malaka'jin, Blood Feeders begin with butchered game drawing Deepmoss spiders toward the trolls' camps. Xen'Zilla asks the Horde to drive the predators back from the settlement. The trolls founded Malaka'jin as a frontier outpost in southeastern Stonetalon Mountains, where they could hunt. The craggy slopes offer plenty of game, but its meat draws nocturnal predators into camp. Deepmoss spiders are aggressive arachnids native to the crags and canyons to the north. Under cover of darkness, they slip in to scavenge the trolls' stores or hunt the hunters themselves. Xen'Zilla asks you to track the predators north into the mountain passes. That will help keep Malaka'jin safe and protect its supplies. Deepmoss Creepers and Venomspitters gather thickest around the rocky ravines and webs of Sishir Canyon. Thin their numbers, and the brood will retreat from the settlement. Then the hunters can rest without fearing an ambush from the shadows.

quest:6462.text: Troll Charm. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa mourns kin slain on the road and seeks their stolen sacred charms. The Thistlefur furbolgs took the talismans into their den. You are at Zoram'gar Outpost, a remote Horde refuge on Ashenvale's western coast. Woodland paths make the way dangerous. A party of Darkspear trolls never arrived after the Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed them. Mitsuwa accepts that his kin have died and will meet him in the afterlife. Yet the furbolgs stole their sacred charms, and he cannot abide the insult. Troll charms and talismans mark identity, give spiritual protection, and bind their bearers to the Loa. Mitsuwa sees a troll without her charm as hollow and worthless, like an orc without battle scars. The Thistlefur furbolgs carried the stolen charms to Thistlefur Hold, deep in the caves beyond Thistlefur Village. There they hid the talismans in chests, far from their rightful owners.

quest:6482.text: Freedom to Ruul. In northern Ashenvale, Ruul waits in a cage deep inside Thistlefur Hold. He needs a Horde ally to help him fight through the corrupted furbolg den and reach safety. Ruul Snowhoof, a druid, is trapped in Thistlefur Hold. While exploring the corrupted woods of northern Ashenvale in bear form, he strayed too close to the den. The corrupted furbolgs had lost their ancestral wisdom and, driven by feral paranoia, mistook him for an ordinary beast. They caged and starved him instead of honoring him, draining his magic until he could no longer break free alone.

quest:65.text: The Defias Brotherhood. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle sends you east to Lakeshire, where a contact may know where the Defias Brotherhood hides. The People's Militia cannot find who directs the bandits. Gryan Stoutmantle needs the cartel's inner circle and its commander exposed before the thieves can be stopped. Wiley the Black waits upstairs at the Lakeshire inn. Stoutmantle trusts the rogue's underworld ties to reveal the Brotherhood's hideouts. Whether Wiley can offer a lead is still uncertain.

quest:6523.text: Protect Kaya. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Kaya Flathoof is held captive among hostile Grimtotem tauren. Horde adventurers guide her along dangerous trails to Camp Aparaje, then tell her anxious father, Makaba Flathoof, that she survived. Kaya Flathoof was captured deep in Grimtotem territory in the Stonetalon Mountains. The tauren clans are divided by bitter rivalries, and few face sharper hostility than the Grimtotem. Kaya has escaped captivity, but friendly ground lies beyond trails watched by enemies and predators. An armed escort gives her the best hope of getting through. Kaya aims for Camp Aparaje in the eastern Stonetalon Mountains. From there, she knows the way home and can continue on her own. You guide her along paths where ambushes threaten, helping her avoid recapture on the way to safety.

quest:6541.text: Report to Kadrak. At the Crossroads, Thork sends proven Horde fighters north to Kadrak's watch tower. The orc prepares recruits for the fighting ahead near the Ashenvale border. The Crossroads faces quilboar, centaur, and local brigands. Beyond it, the Horde looks toward Ashenvale's thick forests. Thork sends fighters who have proved themselves in the central Barrens to the tower on the northern border, where Kadrak is stationed. Kadrak watches the southern approach to Ashenvale and organizes reinforcements for the Horde's foothold across the border. Splintertree Post and an outpost along the Zoram Strand help strengthen the Horde's presence in the timber-rich woodlands. Native night elves resist them fiercely.

quest:6542.text: Report to Kadrak. At Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip sends Horde warriors north to Kadrak's watch post. The journey leads from Stonetalon's crags to Ashenvale, where the Horde holds outposts at Splintertree Post and the Zoram Strand. Darn Talongrip watches the Horde's southern and mountain frontiers from Malaka'jin. The orc sends capable fighters passing through Stonetalon toward the northern Barrens watch tower. Ashenvale is the greater pressure point. There, night elf sentinels clash with Warsong lumber gatherers, and the Horde needs fighters as the struggle for the forest continues. Kadrak oversees Horde troop movements from a watch tower in the northern Barrens, where the savannah meets Ashenvale. The Horde holds outposts at the Zoram Strand in the west and Splintertree Post to the north. Kadrak coordinates supplies and troops, and sends urgent reports across the contested forest.

quest:6543.text: The Warsong Reports. Couriers from the northern Barrens carry Kadrak's orders and gather the Warsong Reports across Ashenvale. Their field observations come from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs this route because the Barrens cannot provide the timber Orgrimmar requires. So the Warsong clan has pressed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help them keep in step. Yet night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails. Warsong scouts watch three parts of Ashenvale. On the western coast, a runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches naga activity and other coastal threats along the Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates the defense against Sentinel raids. Farther east, an outrider watches the road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara. Their reports give Kadrak a view of night elf movements and weaknesses along the frontier.

quest:6544.text: Torek's Assault. At Silverwing Outpost, Torek leads a strike against the night elves. Sent by Splintertree Post, the orc raider means to break Sentinel resistance and kill their commander, Duriel Moonfire, in Ashenvale's border war. Across Ashenvale, the Horde's lumber camps and the native night elves are locked in a growing border war. Torek gathers raiders from Splintertree just outside Silverwing Outpost, aiming to break the Alliance's defenses. He charges before the night elves can counterattack or gather strength for a reinforced campaign against Splintertree Post. Silverwing Outpost is a woodland garrison held by Silverwing Sentinels and fierce elven warriors. Torek sets his sights on their leader, Duriel Moonfire. If she falls, the local night elf command loses its head, and the raiders can report their bloody victory to Ertog Ragetusk at Splintertree Post.

quest:6545.text: Warsong Runner Update. Across Ashenvale, Warsong Runner Update warns of mounting pressure on the Warsong Clan's border. The report alerts commanders to increasingly bold naga attacks on Horde outposts. Across Ashenvale, Warsong scouts and runners watch the fighting and keep supply lines open. Night elf sentinels and the forest make their work dangerous, so frontier commanders need news quickly. Couriers carry dispatches to remote garrisons and to commanders such as Kadrak at the Mor'shan Rampart. Horde defenders expect night elves among the trees, yet outpost sentries report bolder naga attacks. The serpentine invaders strike from waterways and ancient ruins, testing barricades and drawing defenders from forest and border patrols. A dispatch to the Mor'shan Rampart warns of these coordinated assaults from the water.

quest:6548.text: Avenge My Village. Makaba Flathoof calls on Horde travelers to answer the Grimtotem assault in southeastern Stonetalon. He barely escaped, cut off from his kin and surrounded by the dead. Now he seeks vengeance at the camp of the ruffians and hired sellswords. Near the Barrens border, Makaba Flathoof is the lone survivor of a massacre in Stonetalon's red stone passes. Grimtotem raiders struck without warning and slaughtered nearly everyone in his settlement. Makaba fought back and brought down several attackers. Then they drove him into hiding with little more than his life and his wrath. The Grimtotem have long troubled the tauren tribes united under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Unlike Mulgore's peaceful nomads, their warbands use ruthless ruffians and opportunistic mercenaries to seize territory and strike isolated settlements. Makaba has no thought of diplomacy or tribal kinship now. Only blood repaid with blood can answer his grief.

quest:6608.text: You Too Good.. Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to seek his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle. Lumak teaches fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel. So he admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. Artisan fishing calls for knowledge beyond the city and the Horde. Lumak sends you to find his human friend, Nat Pagle. Though the Horde and Alliance clash across Kalimdor, he warns you not to harm or eat Nat. Nat camps on an islet in Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. He keeps clear of politics and cares only whether the fish are biting.

quest:6611.text: To Gadgetzan You Go!. In Orgrimmar, Zamja sends seasoned Horde cooks south to learn from an eccentric goblin butcher. In the Drag, Zamja trains cooks and feeds warriors and travelers passing through Durotar. When a cook has learned every recipe and technique she knows, Zamja has taught all she can. She sends her pupil to Tanaris, where only a master of strange and exotic meats can help a talented cook advance. Gadgetzan is a steam-powered trading hub in Tanaris, run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Dirge Quikcleave works inside the town tavern. The eccentric goblin butcher has an unusual palate and no squeamishness about food. Across Kalimdor, he is known for making hearty meals from monstrous desert creatures and sometimes scraps of leather, food for hardened adventurers.

quest:6623.text: Horde Trauma. At Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Horde Trauma calls skilled healers to the front lines. Doctor Gregory Victor needs hands ready to save lives under extreme pressure. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Arnok, the orc first aid trainer, tells proficient healers they have caught Doctor Gregory Victor's attention. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from Hammerfall in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok regards the summons as the highest step in a battlefield surgeon's career. At Hammerfall, constant skirmishes with Stromgarde's forces and hostile local factions leave Doctor Victor flooded with wounded grunts, raiders, and scouts. The chief physician skips the pleasantries. He sends newcomers into their scrubs to prove their worth in fast, brutal emergency triage.

quest:6625.text:
Alliance Trauma. Across the Alliance, accomplished medics are sent to Theramore Isle for service. There, you study under Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen, chief physician of the Alliance's elite medical corps. Your skill with needle, cloth, and triage has drawn Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen's notice. From Theramore Isle, he leads Alliance Trauma, caring for the wounded in Kalimdor's fiercest warzones and beyond. In Ironforge, Nissa Firestone treats VanHowzen's personal summons as a rare privilege. Theramore Isle faces regional threats, skirmishes, and harsh wilderness, so grievously wounded soldiers arrive in a steady stream.

You cross the sea to Dustwallow Marsh. There, VanHowzen tests how calmly you assess the wounded against his rigorous triage standards.

quest:6629.text: Kill Grundig Darkcloud. At Grimtotem Post, Grundig Darkcloud waits after leading the force that sacked Makaba Flathoof's home. Makaba sends you after Grundig once you have struck down the ruffians and mercenaries. Makaba Flathoof survived the Grimtotem assault on his settlement along the Stonetalon trail, but grief still weighs on him. You have proved yourself against Grimtotem foot soldiers. Now Makaba points you toward Grundig Darkcloud, who led the slaughter that leveled the village and commands a devoted band of brutes. Grundig camps at Grimtotem Post, farther up the mountain road to the west. You climb to the stronghold to avenge Makaba's kin and guard the pass from further violence. There you fight through Grundig's brutes and kill him before his raiders can descend on other vulnerable camps.

quest:6641.text:
Vorsha the Lasher. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Vorsha the Lasher's attacks threaten the Horde's foothold on Ashenvale's coast. The nearby naga honor the hydra with an offering brazier on an offshore island. Muglash means to extinguish its flame and draw Vorsha ashore. On Ashenvale's northwestern coast, Zoram Strand is one of the most dangerous stretches of shore. Zoram'gar Outpost holds a narrow strip there, facing hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Vorsha the Lasher is among the strand's worst threats. The gargantuan hydra strikes the outpost without provocation.

She surges from the surf to crush its defenses and butcher its warriors. Then she vanishes into the deep tides. The nearby naga honor Vorsha's ravenous violence. On a rocky outcrop offshore, they keep an offering brazier burning for her. Muglash, an orc set on ending the outpost's constant harassment, has found a way to draw the hydra out.

Defiling the ritual flame will enrage the naga guardians and Vorsha. In her fury, the hydra will surge to the surface, giving the defenders a chance to draw her into an ambush instead of waiting for another slaughter.

quest:6661.text: Deeprun Rat Roundup. At the Deeprun Tram, Monty asks passing travelers to round up the rats. His flute’s charming melody draws the living Deeprun rats along. Monty keeps pests from overrunning the Deeprun Tram. He speaks in salty sea slang and treats the tramway like a ship’s deck. Vermin scurry through the underground station. So Monty asks travelers passing along the line to help gather them.

quest:6662.text: Me Brother, Nipsy. On the Deeprun Tram, Monty sends live rats to his brother Nipsy in Stormwind. Nipsy runs a rat kabob stall at the far terminal, while Monty's odd manner hints at Gnomeregan's tragedy. At the Ironforge station, Monty asks you to carry live rats through the Deeprun Tram to his brother Nipsy at the Stormwind depot. The short trip links the dwarven and human capitals beneath the mountains. Curious trades carry on along the way. The crate is labeled Carton of Mystery Meat, but inside are live Deeprun rats. Nipsy runs a rat kabob stall at the Stormwind terminal and needs the rats before they spoil. When the crate arrives intact and twitching, he is relieved to have food for travelers passing through the station.

quest:6962.text: Treats for Great-father Winter. At Smokywood Pastures' display in Orgrimmar, the Greatfather Winter performer is tired of hearing holiday wishes. He asks you for gingerbread cookies and milk. The Greatfather Winter who greets visitors in the Valley of Strength works for Smokywood Pastures. Long hours of hearing citizens speak of festive treats leave him hungry. So he asks passing travelers for warm baking and a cold drink. Holiday Spices from Smokywood Pastures peddlers and Small Eggs from wild birds make the cookies. Bring them together with Ice Cold Milk from a local tavern. Then the feast's organizers offer festive cheer and a small token of gratitude.

quest:6984.text: A Smokywood Pastures' Thank You!. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive thanks for the stolen holiday treats you recovered. Great-father Winter waits to honor those who brought Smokywood Pastures' supplies back. In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures sells treats, recipes, and seasonal cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. A shipment was stolen in the snowy hills of the Alterac Mountains, and business stalled. Now the treats are recovered and the Abominable Greench is dealt with. Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive the company's thanks. Great-father Winter waits beside the holiday tree in the Valley of Strength. The goblins have arranged for him to honor those who rescued the holiday supplies. He gives them a seasonal blessing and a Smokywood Pastures Special Gift.

quest:7025.text: Treats for Greatfather Winter. In Ironforge, the dwarf playing Greatfather Winter asks you for a holiday treat. Bring five freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk, and he thanks you with a festive gift. Smokywood Pastures sponsors the Winter Veil festivities in Ironforge. By the holiday tree in the Commons, a performer sits dressed as Greatfather Winter. For hours, he hears holiday wishes from citizens and eager children. He wears the guise of an immortal figure from ancient titan lore and dwarven myth. After hearing requests for gifts all day, the performer grows hungry. He asks for five freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk. The simple meal gives the exhausted festival worker a moment of relief. Your kindness spreads goodwill through Ironforge.

quest:730.text: Trouble in Darkshore?. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker needs help finding his missing crew. His appeal sends you across the sea to Auberdine, where the dwarven expedition met trouble along Darkshore’s wild coast. Darnassus is the grand night elven capital, and home to dwarven researchers from Ironforge who study Kalimdor’s ancient mysteries. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to uncover ancient artifacts. Weeks have passed without word or a progress report. Greywhisker fears dangers have overtaken his field crew. Greywhisker laments that many in the Alliance dismiss dwarven archaeology as an eccentric hobby. Discoveries in Khaz Modan have convinced his colleagues that a terrifying ancient force threatens Azeroth from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. So the work in Darkshore’s ruins is more than scholarship. The expedition seeks to understand historic cataclysms and the deep-seated dangers buried beneath ancient soil.

quest:744.text: Preparation for Ceremony. Eyahn Eagletalon is making a headdress for his brother, who soon stands before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof. He asks you to gather the vibrant feathers from harpies beyond Thunder Bluff while he tans the leather bands. Among the tauren, standing before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof brings pride and reverence. Families honor the occasion by preparing proper attire. The traditional headdress is made from treated leather and symbolic plumage, with each part chosen to show dignity and respect before the leader of the united tribes. A ceremonial headdress needs a leather band and feathers for its crown. While the leather straps are tanned, long, pristine feathers must be gathered. Harpies roost in the craggy hills north and northwest of Thunder Bluff, so you must venture into their hostile nests to find feathers of the needed size and color.

quest:7493.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Orgrimmar, skilled leatherworkers learn how Onyxia's scales can guard against the black dragonflight. Overlord Runthak teaches them a rare cloak-making technique for the flames of Blackrock Spire. Onyxia's fall is a triumph for the Horde, but the black dragonflight remains a threat. Her scaled hide resists draconic flame. So Horde leaders seek craftsmen who can turn the dragon's remains into defensive armor instead of letting them go to waste.

quest:7497.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly honors the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft of making a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can work her hide. When a master leatherworker comes to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer sees how much that skill may matter in battles ahead.

quest:765.text: Supervisor Fizsprocket. In Mulgore, Morin Cloudstalker calls for help against the Venture Company mine. Documents from a ruined caravan show a plan to drive the tauren from their homeland, and Morin needs Supervisor Fizsprocket's clipboard. A Venture Company caravan lies destroyed, and its documents reveal a plan to drive the tauren from Mulgore. The company wants the plains and the veins beneath them for itself. It means to take their resources without the tauren in its way.

quest:770.text: The Demon Scarred Cloak. In Mulgore, The Demon Scarred Cloak carries the wounds of Ghost Howl's torment. The hide came from a legendary white wolf scarred by the Burning Legion. Its arrival in Bloodhoof Village brings the beast's troubled story to a close. Ghost Howl is a legendary white wolf whose sorrowful howl carries across Mulgore. The hide left by the beast bears the scars of demonic corruption. Those marks came from desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion. The wounds lingered in Ghost Howl's flesh and spirit long after the Third War. Mulgore's tauren revere the wild beasts of their homeland as children of the Earth Mother. In Bloodhoof Village, Skorn Whitecloud receives the scarred cloak as proof that the tormented predator is dead. He recognizes the skill it took to track and defeat Ghost Howl. Somberly, he hopes the wolf's tortured spirit has found peace.

quest:776.text: Rites of the Earthmother. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof sends you across Mulgore to track down the great kodo Arra'chea. Even after the old rites, he asks his people to prove their strength, tracking, and devotion anew. Arra'chea's horn shows Cairne you are ready to serve the wider Horde. In Thunder Bluff, a young tauren's childhood gives way to duty. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof asks young hunters to keep proving themselves. Reaching the high bluffs begins a life of service to the United Tauren Tribes. Cairne asks for more than a hunt for small pests: he wants proof of fieldcraft, shown by tracking and cleanly harvesting one of Mulgore's renowned wandering beasts. Arra'chea is a massive, legendary kodo whose looping path crosses the golden grasses northeast of Thunder Bluff. Bringing down this great beast takes patient stalking across the open savannah, not brute force alone. Return Arra'chea's horn to the high rise, and Cairne sends skinners and gatherers to use every part of the sacred beast for the city's provisions.

quest:7781.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head reaches Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives it as proof that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory ranks among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history.
