Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hold a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes the forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. She wants it destroyed.

quest:92819.text: Destruction in Deadmines. Alba Fairmoon sends you against the Defias forge beneath Westfall. The explosives are planted, and she waits in the hills behind Moonbrook with the detonator. Beneath Westfall, the Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength. Alba Fairmoon sends you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are planted beside it. You return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook, where you can set them off from a safe distance. She hopes the blast will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal. Deep in the Deadmines, the charge waits beside the forge. After you rejoin Alba Fairmoon in the hills behind Moonbrook, a remote detonator lets you set it off from outside the caves. She hopes the destroyed forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal.

quest:92834.text: Avenged Tenfold. Elaadrin turns from diplomacy to retribution after the Al'Aketh cult answers his appeal with violence. The High Order scholar had sent his dear friend Belathaan Brightwish to seek peace at the Shrine of Akir, north of Valanaar. The Al'Aketh cult's violence brought armed posturing from factions like the Peacekeepers and Windshapers. Elaadrin spoke for the High Order and saw such displays as a foolish escalation. His order prizes pragmatism and avoids conflict, so he still believed reasoned dialogue could work. He sent his close friend, Belathaan Brightwish, to the Shrine of Akir to negotiate peace. The High Order puts logic before sentiment and holds that avoiding bloodshed is usually the prudent path. Yet Elaadrin shows how cold logic cuts both ways when foes mistake restraint for helplessness. Crackling arcane energy gathers around him. The High Order favors peace, but those who butcher its emissaries face overwhelming retribution.

quest:92840.text: Catching Wind. At the Overlook Standing Stones, the High Order seeks readings that may help save Zephras. Its expedition faces fierce opposition from the Windshapers in the Shen'dar Highlands. The High Order studies the wild elemental flows of the Shen'dar Highlands in hopes of saving Zephras. At the Overlook Standing Stones, its researchers use an Index Esoteria, a tool made to draw data from the great windstone formations. The Windshapers see these probes as profane trespass against the wind. The High Order's expedition and the Windshapers soon clash at the stones. The Windshapers call the study and taking of elemental energy a desecration of their sacred ways. The High Order sees them as narrow in their beliefs, much like the violent Al'Aketh. It will not let their resistance halt its work to save the realm.

quest:92860.text: In Service of Zephras. The High Order now offers Valanaar its full military and diplomatic support against the Al'Aketh cult. Hostile movements across the island have ended its policy of avoiding direct confrontation. The High Order once tried to avoid open conflict with the secretive Al'Aketh cult. Reports of large troop movements and clear hostility have ended that effort. The cultists are mobilizing, and every settlement on the island faces a threat to its peace and safety. So the High Order has chosen to act. It sends an emissary to join with local defenders before the Al'Aketh strike.

quest:92880.text: Return to Valanaar. Yorna's report brings word to Valanaar that the eastern watchtower has held. Its perimeter is stable, and the remaining attackers are being cleared away. After the attack on the outpost, Yorna sends word to Valanaar. The attackers have been broken, and the defenders are clearing away those who remain. You carry Yorna's Report to ease the leaders waiting in town for news. You bring the eastern watchtower's report to Valennia Stormfist in Valanaar. The tower has held, and its perimeter is stable. Valennia gives thanks to the winds, relieved that the frontier remains secure.

quest:92881.text: The High Elder's Request. In Valanaar, High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong calls for help after coordinated assaults strike the region's watchtowers. Reports from the western watchtower point to a hostile cult targeting the local anchor pylons. Coordinated assaults on the western and eastern watchtowers reveal a troubling pattern. What seemed like scattered skirmishes now points to a planned attack on the local anchor pylons. A report from the western watchtower tells how a skypriest revealed the cult's interest in these structures. Now the towers' defense is an urgent concern. The threat to the anchor pylons is growing, so leaders send you to speak with High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. He has a promising lead on the cult's movements and seeks experienced allies to track the enemy. The cult may be preparing a ritual or sabotage.

quest:92909.text: Harvesting the Harvesters. At Saldean's Farm in Westfall, Ozwin Ironsprocket is trapped by haywire harvest golems. The visiting gnome tinkerer needs salvaged parts to build a way out. Ozwin Ironsprocket came south from Ironforge when its workshops heard of haywire harvesters in Westfall. The gnomish engineer believed he could diagnose and recalibrate the farm machines. He hoped to bring peace to the region's farmlands, already troubled by outlaws and now overrun by rampaging harvesters. Near Saldean's Farm, Ozwin found the harvest golems far more violent than his schematics suggested. Their sharp blades and erratic swings drove him into a nearby stable. Trapped there, he cannot safely return to the fields. He needs daring travelers to salvage isosprings and gyrostabilizers from the machines so he can build a device to escape.

quest:92947.text: Making Our Move. At the Shrine of Akir, a strike force moves against the Al'Aketh and their High Priestess. A frontal charge will draw the defenders while the main force approaches from the flank. At the Shrine of Akir, the assault depends on timing and divided forces. A small band of elite fighters charges the front gates to raise the alarm and draw out the defenders. Meanwhile, the commander leads the main strike team in from the flank. Their push divides the defenders' attention and opens a path toward the shrine's leadership. The Al'Aketh defend the Shrine of Akir with armored Guardians, mystical Spiritcallers and martial Blademasters. The strike force must break through their front lines to reach the inner sanctum, where the High Priestess directs her followers. Once the outer defenders are beaten, you meet the force's second-in-command, Hyusaa Quickbreeze, at the shrine steps.

quest:93065.text: Prepare for Battle. The Peacekeepers are gathering in town to march into the surrounding territory. You are called to make your final preparations and meet Valennia Stormfist in the Gustberry Lowlands before the company departs. The Peacekeepers, the local defense forces, have called their troops and volunteers to arms as tensions rise. Secure your equipment, ready your weapons, and join the company as it forms for an organized march into the surrounding territory. The company gathers along the eastern road leading north out of town into the Gustberry Lowlands. There, organizer Valennia Stormfist inspects the fighters and calls the roll. Then the company marches into danger.

quest:93090.text: What Comes Next. On Zephras Isle, the expedition prepares to cross the skies for Kalimdor. The local cult is defeated, and High Elder Shadowsong has given his blessing. Skycutters now carry travelers between the island and Mulgore. High Elder Shadowsong has blessed the expedition's onward journey from Zephras Isle, where the local cult has been defeated and safety restored. The expedition now looks beyond the island, with its focus set on travel across the open skies toward Kalimdor. Ayessa Dawnsinger coordinates the final departure for those ready to leave. Muln worked to secure steady skycutter travel between Zephras Isle and Mulgore. Test voyages succeeded, and an advance party has already crossed over. They wait on the other side to make contact with the shaman of the Earthen Ring.

quest:93159.text: The Strange Hermit. In Shadowgale Forest, a hooded hermit keeps to himself beneath the trees. Though years alone have made him shy, he shares something of his handmade life and the forest spirits who sing to him. Deep beneath Shadowgale Forest's canopy, you find a hooded recluse far from towns and trade routes. He is known simply as the Strange Hermit. Years without ordinary company have left him nervous and awkward in conversation. Even a greeting seems strange to him. The hermit says he has the company and provisions he needs. He once lived elsewhere, then chose a life here among handmade trinkets and the local forest spirits. They often sing to him, though their songs cannot answer him as another person can.

quest:93160.text: The Forest's Bounty. In Shadowgale Forest, a forager needs help gathering fallen acorns. Raptor-like predators prowl the deeper woods, and the harvest can be roasted into a forest meal. A cautious forager in Shadowgale Forest has gathered the acorns near safety. Fierce, raptor-like creatures prowl among the trees and keep the forager from reaching the wilder groves. So passing travelers are needed to gather what lies deeper in the woods, and help ensure neither goes hungry. Shadowgale Acorns make hearty food when prepared with care. Raw, they can be bitter or tough, but roasting them over a fire turns the wild harvest into a rich treat. To gather them, you must brave the timber where predatory birds prowl.

quest:93165.text: Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears. In the wilds around Shadowgale Forest, the Nightclaw survivors seek vengeance against the Al'Aketh. After a terrible tragedy at the cultists' hands, they offer coin and a promise of access to their hidden lore for trophies taken from slain enemies. Their feud now reaches across Shadowgale Forest and the surrounding territories. The Nightclaw enclave and the Al'Aketh cultists are locked in a bitter feud. A terrible tragedy has left the survivors with no hope of peace. They seek vengeance for their fallen kin and turn to wandering adventurers and mercenaries for help. The enclave offers coin and the promise of deeper trust to those who kill cultists and bring back their ears as proof. The Al'Aketh spread their influence through the Gustberry Lowlands, Shadowgale Forest, and the ancient Shrine of Akir. Their dark practices and fanatical ways have earned the hatred of local inhabitants. Striking the cult's camps across these lands can weaken its reach and earn favor with the secretive Nightclaw. The enclave keeps its mysteries close until an outsider proves their loyalty.

quest:93172.text: Free the Hollows. In Shadowgale Forest, the wind hollows’ sorrowful song carries through ancient ruins. An old tragedy binds these ghost-like spirits, and travelers seek to give them peace. Elves across the island have long feared Shadowgale Forest as a haunted grove. In its northeastern woods, old stone ruins lie beneath the overgrowth. Ghost-like wind hollows drift there without rest, but they show no malice. Their sorrow points to a disaster that befell the ruins ages ago. On quiet nights, travelers near the ruins hear strange singing on the breeze. No mortal song sounds like it, and its deep melancholy unsettles those who hear it. Compassionate travelers believe the shades suffer in their endless lament. They seek the wind hollows to break their spectral bonds and grant them peace.

quest:93320.text: Tower Defense. At the fortified position, Tower Defense holds against overwhelming numbers. The defenders have kept the line for now, but exhaustion threatens to break it. The garrison holds back the first assault at a fortified position. Yet the attackers outnumber them and keep pressing forward. The surviving fighters are growing tired, and the line between survival and defeat grows thin. The garrison keeps its perimeter, but time favors the attackers. Prolonged skirmishes against superior numbers drain the defenders’ strength. They need a decisive move to break the stalemate before their lines buckle.

quest:934.text: Crown of the Earth. At the Oracle Glade, Corithras Moonrage sends you to gather water from Teldrassil’s sacred moonwell. The journey begins to reveal why the World Tree’s creation went awry. Corithras Moonrage sends you northwest across Teldrassil to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the Oracle Tree’s great boughs lies the island’s first and most powerful moonwell. You draw water from its sacred pool into an Amethyst Phial. Druids and the tree itself watch over their new homeland’s health from this sanctuary.

quest:935.text: Crown of the Earth. In Teldrassil, moonwell waters are gathered to ease the World Tree’s sickness. The rites carry the samples to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus, where worry grows over a tree raised without blessings. Teldrassil rose after the Third War to give the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. Yet the Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings and would not sanction its making. Without their protection, sickness spreads through the tree. Strange creatures emerge from its boughs, and furbolg tribes once at peace fall into madness.

quest:937.text: The Enchanted Glade. In northwestern Teldrassil, Bloodfeather harpies threaten the Oracle Glade and its ancient Oracle Tree. After they kill a runner bound for Darnassus, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak calls for their nests to be thinned and their belts brought back as proof. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak guards the Oracle Glade with an escort of warriors. At its heart stands the colossal Oracle Tree, an ancient rooted among Teldrassil's boughs. Bloodfeather harpies have spread through the surrounding canopy. They nest in its hollows and threaten anyone who comes near. A runner carrying an urgent report from the Oracle Tree never reaches Darnassus. Bloodfeather harpies ambush and kill the messenger before the runner can leave the glade. Arynia calls on you to thin their flock and bring back Bloodfeather belts as proof that their nests have been weakened.

quest:938.text: Mist. In Teldrassil's shaded boughs, Mist lies wounded and apart from her companion. She needs a safe path to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at a nearby moon well. Mist lies wounded in Teldrassil's undergrowth, her gray coat marked by deep slashes across her back and belly. Her blue eyes remain bright, and she stays calm instead of acting like a feral beast. She looks to friendly travelers for guidance and protection.

quest:93836.text: The Fate of Zephras. After Lorthuna falls, word of danger reaches Valanaar. Zephras Isle's wards have failed, and Ayessa proposes a journey to Azeroth. High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong must hear what has happened. Lorthuna has fallen after the battle above the Shrine of Akir. Yet Zephras Isle has paid dearly for the victory. Its ancient wards, which hid it from Al'Akir, have collapsed. The floating sanctuary now lies exposed in the Windlord's domain. A messenger crosses the isle with word for Valanaar.

quest:93958.text: The Inner Sanctum. At the Shrine of Akir, Valennia Stormfist's assault has gone silent. Her force breached the deepest chamber amid fierce fighting, and now allies outside fear for those within. Valennia Stormfist led her detachment into the inner sanctum of the Shrine of Akir after a hard assault. Fighting sounded from deep within the chambers, fierce and desperate. Then the noise stopped without warning. Allies waiting outside can only fear the worst.

quest:940.text: Teldrassil. After the harpies are driven back, Arynia Cloudsbreak sends you to Darnassus with news for the kaldorei leadership. The inscribed bark tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm what troubles Teldrassil's boughs. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak gives you a piece of inscribed bark after you clear the harpies from their nests in the Oracle Glade. The Oracle Tree watches over the forest, and now Arynia can send word to the kaldorei leadership. You carry her report through the wilderness to Darnassus, the great forest of stone, and deliver it to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Fandral Staghelm receives the report with gratitude and frustration. The harpies have been pushed back, yet one threat gives way to another across Teldrassil. Staghelm championed the planting of the new World Tree to reclaim the night elves' lost immortality. The afflictions in its boughs remind him that his work is far from finished.

quest:941.text: Planting the Heart. At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan care for a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. He clears away its moss, then asks you to place it in his planter and see if it can be healed. Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. So the herbalist trusts his years of tending plants and soil. He asks you to bury the heart in his personal planter, hoping his enriched soil can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

quest:944.text: The Master's Glaive. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu fears the Twilight's Hammer cult has reached the fallen ancient horror. He sends Alliance scouts to investigate. Onu sees corruption linger along Darkshore, driving wildlife from its homes. The naga on the coast trouble him, but signs of the Twilight's Hammer trouble him more. Its followers worship primal lords who ruled the world before their overthrow in ages past. South of Onu, a grim excavation surrounds a colossal creature pierced by a great stone weapon. Onu gives you a Phial of Scrying and asks you to enter the pit and learn whether cultists have gathered there. The behemoth has been dead for eons, yet corruptive power still clings to its bones. The Twilight's Hammer may seek to claim it.

quest:94465.text: Call of Fire. You carry the Torch of the Dormant Flame through Loch Modan to seek Braldir Ashmantle. The trial tests whether an initiate is ready to wield elemental flame. To earn the totem of fire, you carry the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame into the crags of Loch Modan. Beyond the stone carvings of the Valley of Kings, a steep path climbs to an isolated mountain summit. There the elements hold sway, far from the roads travelers know. Braldir Ashmantle watches over the Shrine of the Dormant Flame on a high, windswept peak. Unprepared wanderers and fortune hunters find only silence and bare stone. But when you arrive as a true initiate bearing the sacred torch, Braldir reveals the elemental power sleeping within the shrine's brazier, waiting to be rekindled.

quest:94466.text: Call of Fire. In Loch Modan, initiates seek the Eternal Flame and the fire totem it grants. Braldir Ashmantle guides them through a trial that calls for reagents from kobolds and troggs. They prepare a fire sapta and learn that flame can forge and give life as well as destroy. In Loch Modan, Braldir Ashmantle guides initiates who seek the power of flame. Before they can commune with fire spirits, they must attune their mortal spirits with a sacred draught called a fire sapta. Without it, the Eternal Flame would consume them instead of enlightening them. Braldir asks each petitioner to gather two reagents from hostile valley dwellers and prove their resolve. A fire sapta needs substances rich in elemental power. In the north, Tunnel Rat Geomancers gather sticky fire tar in their warrens to fuel their subterranean magic. In the south, Stonesplinter Seers carry reagent pouches filled with primitive elemental charms across the hills. Claiming these items means facing two of Loch Modan’s most entrenched pests, and gaining what is needed to bind an initiate’s soul to flame. Once the reagents are gathered, Braldir Ashmantle teaches patience alongside the power to destroy. To him, fire means more than fury and ash. It is life, the craft of the forge, and the breath of creation. Mastery calls for balance: shadow gives meaning to light, and flame keeps stone from being only a cold memory. To master fire, an initiate must learn when to blend rather than burn.

quest:94467.text: Call of Fire. At the shrine, an initiate drinks fire sapta to face the trial called Call of Fire. The rite asks them to subdue a spirit and offer its embers to the sacred brazier. An initiate receives prepared fire sapta, guided by elemental lore. The draught awakens their senses to the unseen world. After drinking at the shrine, they climb toward the peak, where mortal sight gives way to primal forces. There, a dormant manifestation of fire awaits their challenge. The Minor Manifestation of Fire tests an initiate's resolve and endurance. It does not attack until challenged, then grows fiercer with each passing moment. When subdued, it yields glowing embers. Carry them to the brazier atop the Shrine of Eternal Flame to kindle the torch and win the spirit's lasting favor.

quest:94468.text: Call of Fire. Above Loch Modan, an initiate kindles the flame that must reach Dun Morogh. Bruegs Kindleborn awaits its return and judges the traveler's command of the elements. An initiate lights the Torch of Eternal Flame on a mountain ridge above Loch Modan. The flame marks the beginning of a deeper bond with the elements. From there, the initiate carries it down the trails and into the snowy vales of Dun Morogh. In Dun Morogh, Bruegs Kindleborn awaits the traveler. He is an elemental mentor who judges whether the traveler's inner fire has taken hold. The blazing torch proves the initiate's will and reverence for fire. Bruegs then grants the Fire Totem, welcoming the flameborn into a lineage of elemental guidance for their kin.

quest:94484.text: Unnerving Silence. In northeastern Shadowgale Forest, a druid enclave has gone silent. Since Ban'aethall fell into ruin, unrest has spread through the territory. After Ban'aethall fell into ruin, unrest stirred through the territory. Regular messages from the druid conclave in a cave in northeastern Shadowgale Forest have now stopped. Their allies have heard nothing, and worry grows as the forest grows more unsettled. You are sent into northeastern Shadowgale Forest to find Elegael Thornpaw, a prominent druid of the enclave. Has the conclave withdrawn deeper into communion with nature, or have the dangers that tore through Ban'aethall reached the cave? No one knows the enclave's fate.

quest:94485.text: Tears of the Lady. In Shadowgale, Lady's Tear moss may keep Elegael's wounded companions alive. They are trapped in Nightclaw Den, and Elegael needs medicine from nearby trees. Elegael needs your help in Shadowgale. Wounded companions are trapped inside Nightclaw Den, critically injured and waiting for aid. Ordinary supplies are scarce, so you gather medicine from the surrounding woods. Their wounds cannot wait. Elegael needs Lady's Tear, a spindly moss clinging to tree bases across Shadowgale. Its secretion is viscous and sticky, with natural antiseptic properties. It seals open gashes and shields traumatic wounds from worsening in the damp wild. With enough moss, Elegael can prepare dressings to stabilize the fallen.

quest:94486.text: Feathers for Binding. In Shadowgale Forest, healers need young shrieklings’ feathers to bind a healing poultice. The usually docile birds now attack travelers, making the plumage dangerous to gather. Field healers in Shadowgale Forest treat grave injuries with moss and antiseptic tree sap. Harsh weather can dry the sap or rob it of its strength. So they bind the poultice with young Shadowgale shrieklings’ feathers, which shield the wound and hold the medicine in place. Gathering the soft feathers has grown dangerous. Young Shadowgale shrieklings are usually docile woodland dwellers, but lately they have turned inexplicably aggressive. Their strong talons can inflict lethal wounds. Now the fledglings strike at passersby. Local caretakers mourn the need to cull young beasts. Yet emergencies threaten the region, and the shrieklings grow more dangerous. Thinning their numbers gathers vital curative materials and curbs a rising threat along forest paths. Each feather is treated with respect, so the beasts’ sacrifice is not wasted.

quest:94487.text:
Unwanted and Unworthy. On Zephras, bloodshed in Shadowgale Forest drives Elegael to seek vengeance and recover stolen heirlooms for the High Elder. The Al'Aketh Cultists ambush the local druids in Shadowgale Forest. Elegael had thought these zealots harmless dreamers, with clouds between their ears. Now druid blood stains the forest floor, and Elegael demands swift retribution against the Footsoldiers and Stormchasers responsible. Elegael believes the cultists' betrayal has cost them their heritage. They no longer deserve the name shen'dorei, nor do their remains deserve the winds of their homeland. Many were young, their promising futures cut short by fanaticism.

Their bloodied heirlooms must return to the High Elder. There, the sacred items await a wiser and more worthy generation.

quest:94488.text: The Ties That Bind. Elegael Thornpaw faces a traitor among Shadowgale Forest’s druids. Haalien vanished months ago, then joined the attacking cultists and rose to command them. Now Elegael orders his execution. Druids face a vicious cultist attack in Shadowgale Forest. Elegael Thornpaw finds Haalien’s scent over the slaughter. Haalien was a druid of the circle who vanished months ago, but he did not perish in the wilds. He joined the invading cultists and now commands their violent campaign against his former kin.

quest:94489.text: The Wounds of Betrayal. In Shadowgale Forest, Elegael cares for the shen'dorei druids wounded in a terrible assault. Poultices are ready for Nightfang Den, north across the clearing, while her mate Jorel Windsinger is missing. Elegael tends the shen'dorei druids hurt in the assault on Shadowgale Forest. She has prepared poultices for her brethren sheltering in Nightfang Den, just north across the clearing. Few shen'dorei druids remain, and every survivor matters to their fragile enclave.

quest:94490.text: Ripped Missive. Haalien bears a bloodied letter after an attack on a druid den in Shadowgale Forest. Its words reveal what the cultists sought and point toward danger within Valanaar. Haalien's missive gives a glimpse of the violence in Shadowgale Forest. Found after a fierce skirmish, the torn scrap bears grim news of cultists who attacked a local druid den. Its words offer clues to those seeking justice for the fallen.

quest:94491.text: The Fate of the Den. At the druid den, survivors mourn their fallen after the cultist assault. The Fate of the Den reaches Lotheluum in Valanaar with a recovered missive and word of heavy losses. The dispatch reveals that someone in Valanaar has been feeding vital information to the enemy. Cultists struck the druid den and left its defenders battered and grieving for fallen comrades. Outside aid brought the immediate danger under control, but the physical and emotional devastation remains immense. The dead cannot be brought back, and the wounded survivors are too weak for the long trek. Lingering cultists still roam nearby.

quest:945.text: Therylune's Escape. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Therylune needs help reaching safety. She wandered into the dig sites, and her sister Therysil waits at the Shrine of Aessina, worried for her. At the Master's Glaive, Twilight's Hammer cultists have pinned Therylune down. An ancient monstrosity's skull dominates the ravine, pierced by a huge stone blade. Despite the dread around it, Therylune wandered into the valley's heart. She survives by reacting quickly and hiding among the rough terrain. Therysil waits far to the south at the Shrine of Aessina. Her adventurous sister Therylune rarely minds getting dirt on her clothes, but even Therysil was shocked to hear she had ventured into the unwholesome excavations at the Master's Glaive. Tell her Therylune is safe, and her worry will ease. Therysil knows the dark forces digging through Darkshore's ancient earth.

quest:94568.text: The Cult's True Plans. The cult's informant has died before sharing what he knew. Talaanis Shadowsong must help investigators find another way to oppose the cult. A frightened insider left the cult and hoped to seek help beyond it. Before he could reveal what he knew, he was killed. His warnings remain, but the cult's plans do not.

quest:947.text: Cave Mushrooms. In Darkshore, Cave Mushrooms are needed for a potion Barithras Moonshade prepares in Auberdine. He asks you to gather rare fungi behind Cliffspring Falls and investigate warnings from the Grove of the Ancients. Barithras Moonshade needs scaber stalks and a death cap for a potent mixture. Both grow in a damp cavern behind Cliffspring Falls in northeastern Darkshore. Gathering them is more dangerous than picking ordinary woodland herbs.

quest:948.text: Onu. Barithras Moonshade sends you south from Auberdine to consult Onu. Your findings at Cliffspring Falls have caught the notice of one of Darkshore’s oldest guardians. Barithras Moonshade sees more than strange fungi in the samples you brought to Auberdine. The caves beneath Cliffspring Falls are tainted, and word of them has reached Onu, an Ancient of Lore in the Grove of the Ancients south of town. Darkshore’s waterways may be corrupted beyond anything a naturalist can explain. Onu seeks counsel, and even an Ancient’s patience cannot hide the weight of his summons. The road south from Auberdine turns inland, away from the coastal ruins and toward the mountain slopes. The Grove of the Ancients shelters an old refuge of nature, apart from the decay along the shore. Onu waits among stone barrows and kindred spirits. He is ready to guide allies toward the blights stirring at the edge of the wilderness.

quest:94896.text: Aid For The Refugees. After Ban'aethal fell, its survivors have little left to call their own. The settlement deep in Shadowgale Forest began to fall into the sky in the middle of the night, and danger keeps the refugees from retrieving what they left behind. Ealaane and the other refugees fled their homes deep in Shadowgale Forest. With almost nothing gathered around them, they ask travelers to brave the dangers they left behind. Ban'aethal began to fall into the sky in the dead of night. Its inhabitants had only moments to escape, leaving their personal possessions behind. The surrounding woods grew hostile and dangerous.

quest:94897.text: The Fate of a Loved One. Resaan has been gone from the Ruins of Ban'aethal for more than a week, and his partner waits for news. Travelers bound there are asked to bring him home or return his cherished heirloom. Resaan's partner pleads with him to stay as he prepares to return to the Ruins of Ban'aethal. Yet he feels compelled to brave the ruins for supplies. His partner is left waiting for word. More than a week has passed since Resaan set out, far longer than a swift return should take. His partner asks travelers bound for Ban'aethal to search the ruins. If Resaan lives, bring him home. If tragedy has taken him, recover his family heirloom.

quest:949.text: The Twilight Camp. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, cultists gather while Alliance scouts seek their purpose. A scrying bowl has revealed their ritual site. Now you enter the excavation to learn what the Twilight's Hammer seeks beneath the earth. The Twilight's Hammer has made the Master's Glaive a threat. A scrying bowl revealed the cultists' fortifications. You enter their camp to learn their designs before the Alliance can prepare its defenses.

quest:94947.text: Welcome to Azeroth. You arrive in Stormwind through the Skyborne Portal and are welcomed by its regent. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon grants you leave to travel across Alliance lands. You step through the Skyborne Portal into Stormwind, the human capital. From there, you make your way along the city's grand thoroughfares to Stormwind Keep, where the regency awaits your arrival. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives the arriving members of the High Order in the throne room. A Kirin Tor courier had warned him they were coming. It has been some time since high elves walked the halls of Stormwind Keep, yet Bolvar welcomes them as guests and grants them free passage across Alliance territories on behalf of the King.

quest:950.text: Return to Onu. You bring a torn page from the Twilight Tome to Onu in Darkshore. The cultists' writing is all you could bear to take from their book. The Twilight Tome overwhelms anyone who tries to read it. Its words swim across the page, and its ornate scrollwork twists into grotesque figures. You tear out a page of scribbles before the strain brings on vertigo.

quest:95065.text: Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray keeps to his fishing line while the fish are biting. His supplies run low, so he asks passersby to fetch nightcrawlers and a shiny bauble from a shop along the city canals. Gilbert Gray watches his bobber dance on the water. The elderly angler will not leave his prized perch while the fish are biting. His supplies have run out, and he needs help so he can stay at his line instead of returning to the city. Catherine Leland runs a tackle shop beside Stormwind's stone canals, just west of the Trade District. Fishermen across the city come to her for lures and bait. Her shop can replenish what Gilbert Gray needs to keep fishing.

quest:952.text: Grove of the Ancients. An urgent dispatch takes you from Darnassus to Darkshore, where Onu waits in the Grove of the Ancients. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm sends you across the sea with a message for the Ancient of Lore, who lives south of Auberdine. After you help at the Oracle Glade atop Teldrassil, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm calls you to another duty. He sends you across the sea to Darkshore with an urgent dispatch for Onu. From Darnassus, you can take a hippogryph flight. South of Auberdine, you reach the Grove of the Ancients and deliver the message to Onu. The towering Ancient of Lore accepts it quietly and remarks on Staghelm's impatience. Onu and the forest's ancient keepers believe all things unfold in their proper time. Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage embodied that patient wisdom, while Staghelm lacks it.

quest:953.text:
The Fall of Ameth'Aran. At Ameth'Aran in Darkshore, you search the ruins and read their ancient stone tablets for Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Their words tell how the Highborne city fell in the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine. Ameth'Aran was home to Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who wielded powerful arcane magic. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city fell to broken marble and cracked pillars. The Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins as restless, anguished spirits. Few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact. The War of the Ancients drove night elves into a struggle for survival, and much of their history was lost. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade surveyed Ameth'Aran and found two large engraved tablets, the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran.

Ghostly Highborne specters drove Tysha from the ruins. Their readings can carry the disaster's history to the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

quest:95349.text:
The Earthen Ring. From Zephras, the Windshapers of The Earthen Ring reach Azeroth as an advance vanguard. After cult activity delays the rest in Valanaar, they board a skycutter outside the lodge and make landfall in Mulgore to meet Alaana Stormwalker and adjust to a vast, dangerous world. Cult activity in Valanaar has disrupted the Windshapers’ plans to travel to Azeroth. Their senior leaders stay behind at the lodge to finish urgent business and quell the threat, while a small vanguard sets out ahead. At the docks just outside the lodge, the pioneers board a skycutter bound across the skies.

Their commanders promise to join them soon. Until then, the advance group must establish a presence before the rest can follow. In Mulgore, Alaana Stormwalker welcomes the arriving adventurers from Zephras. Establishing a foothold in Azeroth will take time, so newcomers are encouraged to scout the surrounding territory and grow accustomed to it.

The winds favor the expedition, but Azeroth is unfamiliar and perilous. Travelers should learn the local terrain, wildlife, and neighboring inhabitants before those still in Valanaar arrive to join them.

quest:95350.text: Welcome to Azeroth. In Kalimdor, the Windshapers reach beyond their isolated home to seek allies. Guided by their ties to the Earthen Ring, an emissary travels from Thunder Bluff to meet Warchief Thrall in Orgrimmar. The Windshapers look beyond their isolated origins to the peoples of Kalimdor. They know isolation cannot shield them from Azeroth’s threats, so they seek companions to face the wilderness together. Their search reaches the neighboring tauren city of Thunder Bluff and the orcish bastions to the east. The envoys travel first to the soaring towers of Thunder Bluff, then across the barrens to Orgrimmar, the Horde’s capital. Warchief Thrall waits in the tranquil Valley of Wisdom. An audience with him draws the Windshapers into Kalimdor’s political and spiritual life, joining them to the Horde through shared purpose and respect for the elements.

quest:954.text: Bashal'Aran. An eerie blue aura burns above a shrine in Bashal'Aran, where satyrs and grells will not go. Thundris Windweaver, Auberdine's elder, asks you to find its source. Bashal'Aran once flourished under the ancient Kaldorei Empire. Now demonic taint fills its broken marble halls and overgrown arches. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed on the ruins' lingering magic, growing more malicious by the day. Yet Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine has noticed a mystery: atop a western bluff, a blue aura shines above a shrine that no demon will approach.

quest:95494.text: Bruised Pride and Lion Hides. An injury leaves a hunter or tradesperson unable to gather lion hides for a local tanner. They turn to you to keep their trade agreement and their professional record intact. A hunter or tradesperson has been hurt and cannot safely track wild beasts. Their agreement with a neighborhood craftsman is still due, so they hire you to hunt wild lions and gather their pelts. The raw hides go to a local tanner, who exchanges them for finished leather goods the giver needs for their livelihood. The giver’s pride is stung by needing help, but honoring the bargain keeps their professional reputation unbroken.

quest:95495.text: The Hermit Tanner. You carry raw hides across the Barrens to The Hermit Tanner, who lives above the Dry Hills. Vrang cannot make the climb, so he sends you to his secluded trading partner. Across the Barrens, Vrang trades with a tanner who lives on a ridge above the Dry Hills. The steep, rocky climb is too hard for Vrang, so he asks passing travelers to carry raw hides to his partner's homestead. Vrang warns you that the solitary tanner's unusual appearance may startle you, but says he is no danger to visitors. When you bring the hides to the ridge, the hermit welcomes you warmly. He regrets that Vrang could not come himself, for there is something he hoped to discuss with the trader.

quest:955.text: Bashal'Aran. Magic still binds Asterion beneath Bashal'Aran's broken stones. The ancient night elf seeks release from his ghostly form and suspects the grells have touched the seal that holds him. He asks travelers to gather their earrings and trace its lingering magic. For centuries, Asterion has waited among Bashal'Aran's shattered marble. The ancient night elf spirit remains caught between life and true death beneath Darkshore's canopy. Arcane craft binds him to the ruined settlement, and he cannot break free alone. Solitude and despair have worn down his mind. Asterion believes an ancient seal hidden in the ruins may hold the key to his release. He cannot search the brush and fallen stones himself. The feral grells of Bashal'Aran forage there and steal small baubles, so he asks travelers to gather their earrings. He hopes the trinkets' lingering magic will lead him to the seal that torments his soul.

quest:956.text:
Bashal'Aran. Among the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran, Asterion seeks release from his prison. He has traced the binding magic to the satyrs who command the grells. Now he asks travelers to recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For more than a thousand years, Asterion has been bound within the ruins of Bashal'Aran. The marble pillars mark the bounds of his prison. His strength and ancient magic cannot carry him beyond them. A cursed relic holds him there.

Through the centuries, Asterion has watched Darkshore's canopy. He wonders if the worn stone around him might ever set him free. Nearby grells bore traces of the magic binding Asterion. From them, he reasoned that the Ancient Moonstone Seal was the enchantment's source. The satyrs who command the grells hold the seal now. These demonic night elves roam the ancient groves and keep watch over the relic. Asterion needs travelers to recover the seal so its binding power can be broken.

quest:95621.text: Trouble in the Valley. A squad of Kul Tiran soldiers is searching the valley, and their purpose is unknown. They have camped near a wrecked caravan to the south, drawing the attention of local scouts. A rifleman watching the lowlands spotted human soldiers searching the valley floor. Through his scope, he recognized the heraldry and livery of Kul Tiras. Armed foreigners rarely work so openly here, and their presence has raised alarm. The soldiers have camped near a ruined caravan to the south. What they seek among the wreckage remains unknown. Local observers consider their armed presence an immediate concern, so investigators are sent to eliminate them and uncover the purpose of their search.

quest:957.text: Bashal'Aran. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion's spirit remains bound by an ancient seal. You carry the seal south to Ameth'Aran, where an old flame may break his bonds. The Ancient Moonstone Seal was forged by Highborne sorcerers before the Great Sundering, and no ordinary strength can break its power. Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister settlements of the kaldorei under Queen Azshara, when the Well of Eternity anchored their empire. Now both are overgrown, haunted ruins, where ghosts linger and arcane power remains volatile. At Ameth'Aran, a mystical brazier burns with cyan fire in a stone gazebo; that is the sole flame able to consume the Ancient Moonstone Seal.

quest:959.text: Trouble at the Docks. In Ratchet, a stolen bottle puts Bigglefuzz's job at risk. Mad Magglish fled inland with a 99-Year-Old Port, a gift from Baron Revilgaz to Gazlowe, and now hides in the Wailing Caverns. Ratchet's docks carry sea trade with Booty Bay across the Great Sea. One morning, a huge shipment arrived, and Crane Operator Bigglefuzz overloaded his crane to unload it faster. The crane dropped the whole load across the docks. In the confusion, Mad Magglish, a local nuisance, snatched a valuable bottle of liquor and fled inland. The bottle is a 99-Year-Old Port, a personal diplomatic gift from Baron Revilgaz, Booty Bay's ruler, to Gazlowe, Ratchet's chief engineer and overseer. Its loss could humiliate Bigglefuzz and anger both trade leaders. Fearing for his job or worse, Bigglefuzz followed the thief to the mouth of the Wailing Caverns. But fear stopped him from going inside. Mad Magglish hides in damp natural tunnels outside the Wailing Caverns' inner gateway, not deep in the corrupted dreamscape. The thief relies on clumsy stealth and dark alcoves, hoping pursuers will give up. Find Magglish in the outer caverns before the port is uncorked or destroyed.

quest:96139.text: The Valor Family. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi seeks records of Raven Hill's lost people. The village remembers their courage, but her library holds little of Raven Hill's history. Sirra Von'Indi says brave people helped Darkshire endure. Lady Althea was among them, as were those who died at Raven Hill. You are asked to search for anything that might preserve their memory.

quest:962.text: Serpentbloom. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Serpentbloom draws Apothecary Zamah’s attention. She seeks more specimens for the Royal Apothecary Society’s research and the Forsaken. Apothecary Zamah watches the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff’s Spirit Rise. She came from the Undercity as an envoy of the Royal Apothecary Society. Her tauren hosts tend to spiritual balance and the wounded land, while Zamah studies rare and virulent materials. She has isolated a sample of Serpentbloom and seeks more for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken’s research. Serpentbloom grows in the damp, twisting grottos of the Wailing Caverns, far from the Barrens’ open sun. The corrupted druids of the Fang have twisted these humid depths, where serpentine denizens guard the plant. Many scouts sent by Zamah failed to return. Now she seeks hardy adventurers to gather more.

quest:963.text: For Love Eternal. In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to ease Anaya Dawnrunner's torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has lasted since the city fell. Ten thousand years ago, the War of the Ancients tore Kalimdor apart around the Well of Eternity. Ameth'Aran fell, and Anaya Dawnrunner was lost to Cerellean Whiteclaw. Grief-stricken, Cerellean joined Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage in the druids' long hibernation. He hoped the ages spent walking the Emerald Dream would quiet his heart, but his sorrow endured. When he awoke, Cerellean wandered Darkshore in a stupor. At last he came to the melancholy ruins of Ameth'Aran, where he saw Anaya's tortured ghost. He cannot raise a weapon against the woman he loved. So he asks passing travelers to destroy her tormented form, retrieve her pendant, and bring peace to her troubled soul.

quest:96390.text: Nip 'Em in the Bud. Dark Iron spies move through Dun Morogh, and Earthseer Farsen calls for help. Near Ironband's Compound, their presence threatens the Bronzebeard homeland. Dark Iron spies have crossed Dun Morogh's high passes and snowy crags. They hide near settlements and excavations, where even a few watchers may signal a strike. Earthseer Farsen sees the danger and calls on Alliance defenders to find them before their plans advance.

quest:96391.text: Underground Map. Near Ironband's Compound, the Underground Map points toward chambers beneath Ironforge. Recovered from Dark Iron spies, its runes trace a hidden route piercing toward ancient halls beneath the mountain. You bring it to Earthseer Farsen to begin learning what lies below. You find the parchment near Ironband's Compound after dealing with Dark Iron spies. Its diagrams lay out an intricate maze of roads beneath the earth. Harsh, jagged runes mark passages that run deep underground and converge beneath Ironforge. Their course suggests a possible threat beneath the Bronzebeard capital, though the Dark Iron notes remain uncertain.

quest:96392.text: Farsen's Watch. Near Gol'Bolar Quarry, Earthseer Farsen watches for Dark Iron movement close to Ironforge. The Wildhammer shaman lends you his farsight, revealing a threat that calls for swift action. From his post above Gol'Bolar Quarry, Farsen watches the lower reaches of Dun Morogh. He came south from the crags of Aerie Peak, bringing a Wildhammer's spiritual awareness with him. His clan's old arts let him sense tremors underground and watch for sudden movement along the hillsides. Farsen lends you his farsight, a shamanic gift that carries sight across great distances. Through it, you see danger beyond troggs and wild beasts. Dark Iron dwarves have drawn close to Ironforge's industrial center and are digging in. Their foothold must be confronted before it takes root.

quest:96393.text: Old Ironforge Incursion. Beneath Ironforge, Earthseer Farsen sends you to the Hall of Thanes for the last part of the investigation. There, you face the Dark Iron threat and report to King Magni Bronzebeard. The underground map reveals Dark Iron movements, and Earthseer Farsen identifies the mastermind behind the intrusion. The entrance to the Hall of Thanes lies deep within Old Ironforge's ancient stone halls. While the upper city tends to matters on the surface, Dark Iron forces slip into caverns that lie dormant beneath the kingdom.

quest:96394.text: The Restless Dead. Beneath the Hall of Thanes, restless spirits trouble the crypts where generations of dwarven dead lie at rest. The caretakers fear to enter the vaults, and the disturbance has reached the spirit of Anvilmar. Generations of honored dwarves rest in the ancestral crypts beneath the Hall of Thanes. Their spirits usually sleep in peace, but something unseen has stirred them violently. Strange noises rise from the lower vaults and frighten the caretakers. They will not enter those chambers or perform their duties until order returns. Now adventurers are called to quiet the agitated souls.

quest:96395.text: An Ancient Grudge. Within the Hall of Thanes, Faldrim Anvilmar's spirit remains troubled by an old grievance. His ghostly attendant asks travelers to bring him peace. A ghostly attendant remains in the Hall of Thanes, where Faldrim Anvilmar once ruled. The spirit can barely speak across the veil between the living and the dead. It asks you to quiet its master's restless spirit. It seeks peace for him, not freedom for itself.

quest:96403.text: Important Heirlooms. In the Hall of Thanes, Dark Iron dwarves break into the vaults while Thom is caught inside. The nervous gnome asks you to gather the scattered dwarven relics before the invaders reach them. Thom is a gnome caught in the Hall of Thanes when Dark Iron dwarves tunnel up in mole machines. He cannot secure the vaults alone, so he asks passing adventurers to enter the hostile dig site. The dwarven relics lie scattered through the chambers. The invaders may seize or destroy them.

quest:96408.text: A Visitor to Dun Morogh. Beldin Steelgrill sends you to learn who has lit a fire above Gol'Bolar Quarry. The camp overlooks the excavation, and the dwarves fear its visitor may mean them harm. High on the snowy ridges east of Kharanos, a stranger's campfire burns above the quarry. The unfamiliar fire has worried the folk of Kharanos. There, the Mountaineers watch the heights for danger.

quest:965.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. North of Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze fears trouble at an ancient ruin. She sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the Tower of Althalaxx, but his report has not come. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze keeps watch for danger around Auberdine. Suspicious activity near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore caught her attention, so she sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the ancient ruin. Days have passed without word. Elissa asks you to travel north, find Balthule, and make sure he has not met an untimely end.

quest:966.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Warlocks gather at the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, drawing Balthule Shadowstrike's watchful eye. He asks travelers to recover scraps of parchment from the fanatics camped outside the ruins, hoping to learn who they are and what they seek. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the misty shore of northern Darkshore and keeps the ancient Tower of Althalaxx in sight. Auberdine sent him to watch the ruin and warn Delgren the Purifier if danger grows. Yet leaving his post to report might let the dark spellcasters among the stones slip from view. So Balthule asks passing travelers to scout the camps around the tower.

quest:967.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Dark Strand cultists gather, and Balthule Shadowstrike needs help. He sends a warning with an Alliance courier to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale for his mentor, Delgren the Purifier. Balthule Shadowstrike sees that one scout cannot face the Dark Strand threat alone. After clashing with cultists near the Tower of Althalaxx, he writes a report for his master, Delgren the Purifier, and gives it to an Alliance messenger. The cult's summoners grow bolder. Balthule needs seasoned leaders to direct a response. Balthule's dispatch sends you south along Darkshore's coastal road, then across the wooded border into Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier is stationed at Maestra's Post beside the western road. The human paladin works to cleanse demons and undead from the woodland. Night elven customs once seemed strange to him, but he has earned the Sentinels' deep respect as an indispensable ally.

quest:968.text:
Tools of the Highborne. Thundris Windweaver sends you from Auberdine to Ameth'Aran. Highborne spirits still haunt the ruins with enchanted relics in their hands, and he wants them taken away. Ameth'Aran lies south of Auberdine and east of the coastal highway. Its stone foundations are overgrown. Ten thousand years ago, it was a stronghold of the Highborne, the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire.

Their unchecked arcane magic helped bring about the Sundering, which shattered the settlement. Yet its inhabitants never truly left. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report Highborne ghosts in the sunken plazas, still clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they held in life. For the kaldorei, arcane magic recalls a danger that nearly destroyed life on Azeroth. Thundris Windweaver fears that the Highborne implements could invite corruption if they remain in ghostly hands. So he sends you to wrest the relics from the restless spirits. He intends to have them destroyed before their tainted magic can fuel another disaster.

quest:96877.text: Halikor's Hoof. In the wilds, Halikor's Hoof is carried to Orgrimmar as proof of a hunter's triumph. The enormous severed hoof honors the hunter's victory over the formidable lizard. Halikor's vast size is plain in the hoof taken from its remains. Hunters and warriors in the wilds have long claimed a piece of a formidable beast to prove the kill. The hoof leaves no doubt of the lizard's great size and strength. The heavy hoof is carried to Orgrimmar to announce the beast's defeat to the Horde. Strength and survival against the land's harsh predators matter in this warrior society. Presenting the trophy honors the hunter and assures the capital that a dangerous creature has been slain.

quest:96895.text: The Argent Emissary. In Tirisfal Glades, two Argent Dawn emissaries hunt Scourge cultists near the Undercity. Both are Forsaken, yet local authorities distrust an armed neutral order in their territory. Two Forsaken emissaries of the Argent Dawn have recently reached Tirisfal Glades. Their arrival puts local authorities on edge. The Argent Dawn fights the Scourge, but the Forsaken distrust an armed neutral order acting without oversight in their territory. Even their shared heritage does little to ease that wariness. The emissaries pursue Scourge cultists southeast of the Undercity, near its outskirts. They mean to root out the Lich King's agents before the cultists gain a foothold. One emissary watches their movements from near the city gates.

quest:96896.text: A Righteous Cause. Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr meet again to remember the Undercity's defense against Naxxramas. They speak of Garek Bandarion, a fallen undead hero who found the Holy Light again as a paladin, and of the Forsaken who carry his path onward. Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr meet again after defending Lordaeron together. They survived Naxxramas's assault on the Undercity, though many comrades fell. Now they remember the dead and the hard road faced by Forsaken who still honor the Holy Light. Leonid and Danitha remember Garek Bandarion, the fallen hero whose name was given to the keep. Leonid believes Garek may have been the first Forsaken to wield the Holy Light again as a true paladin. Most Forsaken have turned from the Light. Danitha and her cohort keep Garek's legacy alive and explore what holy unlife may allow. After speaking with Danitha, Leonid prepares to leave the keep and return to the fight against the Scourge in the ravaged east. He is stationed at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. There, he welcomes able-bodied adventurers ready to take up arms.

quest:96897.text: The Cult of the Damned. In Tirisfal Glades, living servants of the Scourge threaten the people once more. By culling Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers, you help keep the Lich King's agents from repeating the betrayals that shattered Lordaeron. The Scourge has living servants who swear fealty to the Lich King. They serve where the mindless dead cannot. In Tirisfal Glades, people already face roaming undead and the relentless zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Now, newly discovered cells of Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers show the Scourge seeking a foothold again. The marching dead were not the only cause of Lordaeron's fall. Neighbors betrayed neighbors as the Cult of the Damned infiltrated villages and poisoned granaries. From the shadows, they helped bring the kingdom down. Fresh Cult activity in Tirisfal threatens to repeat that history in the scarred lands of the north.

quest:96898.text: Remnants of War. Across Tirisfal Glades, remnants of war lie scattered beneath the soil. Naxxramas was driven from the Undercity at great cost to the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn. Its shattered necrotic focusing crystal remains a danger, and Scourge cultists seek its fragments for the dark magic within. Naxxramas once loomed over Tirisfal Glades, seeking to wipe out the Undercity and the Forsaken. The Forsaken and the Argent Dawn fought off the floating fortress in a desperate defense. Both sides suffered heavy losses. During the battle, the immense necrotic focusing crystal atop Naxxramas was destroyed, scattering fragments across the glades. Naxxramas was driven away, but pieces of its crystal remain in the soil. Scourge cultists search for the fragments, hoping to use the dark magic still within them. Gathering the shards keeps that power from the Scourge. Yet clearing every fragment from Tirisfal will take years.

quest:96899.text: Bandarion Keep. At Bandarion Keep, Commander Leonid Barthalomew waits for travelers in western Tirisfal Glades. The Argent Dawn once held the secluded fortress against the Scourge, and Danitha and her paladins now guard its walls. After you aid the Argent Dawn against Cult of the Damned activity, you are sent northwest across Tirisfal Glades. Commander Leonid Barthalomew waits at the fortress to speak with you about the order's ongoing crusade against darkness. The Argent Dawn once used the stronghold as a staging post against Scourge incursions across Tirisfal Glades. Then the order turned its focus to the Eastern and Western Plaguelands. The fort was left behind and began to decay, until Paladin Danitha and her companions took stewardship of its walls.

quest:97220.text: Philmor's Favor. A delicate shipment is bound for the Gatehouse in Stormwind under Philmor's Favor. With dockhands scarce, travelers carry it to a stockroom entrance above Trias' Cheese in the Trade District. Stormwind's freight handlers are short of dockhands, and ordinary cargo schedules are strained. They rely on trustworthy travelers to carry sensitive crates into the city's commercial quarter and keep deliveries moving. The Gatehouse shipment is bound for an unusual destination. Carry the crate to the second floor of Trias' Cheese in the Trade District, where a concealed entrance opens onto a stockroom. Supplies and ceremonial gifts for the guard's officers pass through there, beyond prying eyes.

quest:97222.text: Gatehouse Goods. In Stormwind, Gatehouse Goods moves from Trias' Cheese to the neighboring gatehouse. The route takes the shipment up the shop's stairs to a landing on the same floor, where guards can collect it outside the stockroom. Shared quarters link the city's shops and defenses. Couriers carry a gatehouse shipment up the stairs inside Trias' Cheese. The cheese shop is a separate business with its own inventory, yet its building shares a floor with the neighboring gatehouse. From the upper landing, couriers can move supplies between the two quarters without using the front avenues. The crate is left outside the stockroom door rather than carried inside. Gatehouse guards watch for deliveries and arrange for someone to collect each package when returning to their posts. The door opens inward, so a crate outside will not block the entry or hinder anyone inside.

quest:97234.text: Reading Room. At Roy's Book Club, members trade older literature for newer works from the Stormwind library. Wrapped books carry the exchange between the club and the librarian. Roy's Book Club gathers readers in Stormwind to discuss classical legends and provocative writings. To keep those talks fresh, members rotate their reading. They trade older or less popular works for newer volumes from the city's library. Roy's Book Club keeps an established lending arrangement with the Stormwind library. Roy wraps the club's returned books in a distinctive way, and you carry them to the librarian. In return, the club receives a new list of modern tomes.

quest:97237.text: Shelf Picked. In Stormwind, Roy Lewells sends a runner to gather books for a reading group in the Park. Roy Lewells has sent a note asking for several books from the Stormwind library. The librarian checks the list and confirms every title is in stock. The books are there for you to find and pull from the shelves. The librarian stays at the desk to keep the inventory records. Roy Lewells's note makes you an official courier, so you are not responsible for returning the borrowed books. That duty belongs to Lewells's establishment. Once you bring the volumes to the Park, Roy prepares them for lively after-hours discussions in a cellar. The books have an exotic smell.

quest:97242.text: Yelmak's Medley. Tensions rise in Yelmak's Alchemy and Potions, in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Master alchemist Yelmak hopes a calming mixture made with local water plants will quiet his apprentice Whuut's clumsy frustration and stubborn pride. At Yelmak's Alchemy and Potions, young apprentice Whuut's pride is making trouble. Rather than ask for help when he is out of his depth, he breaks the shop's equipment in frustration. Master alchemist Yelmak seeks to calm the youth without bruising his fragile ego, so he devises a soothing concoction. The recipe calls for fresh cattails and speargrass from the watercourses winding through the Valley of Honor. Kor'geld cannot leave the shop without alerting the suspicious apprentice, so someone discreet must gather the plants. The botanical mixture is meant to temper Whuut's attitude and restore peace to the alchemy shop.

quest:97246.text: Meal Appeal. In Orgrimmar, Thatog worries his young son Migi is skipping meals to play. He asks you to fetch lunch from Borstan's Firepit and find Migi behind Grommash Hold. Thatog's daily duties keep him at his post in Orgrimmar. He has little time to watch Migi, his energetic young son. From morning until dusk, Migi races through the city with his friends. He often ignores his hunger until he comes home famished. Thatog arranges a hot lunch for Migi at Borstan's Firepit and asks you to carry it. Migi would rather keep playing than stop to eat. So you take the meal to the yard behind Grommash Hold, where Migi and the neighborhood children play.

quest:97249.text: Favorite Food. In Orgrimmar, Migi's parents worry that play keeps him from eating enough. Borstan of Borstan's Meats prepares varied lunches with a taste Migi loves, so he and his friends stop to eat. Behind Grommash Hold, young Migi and his friends spend their afternoons playing along Orgrimmar's dusty paths. His parents worry that he often neglects his meals and does not eat enough. So they ask Borstan's Meats to prepare daily packed lunches. They insist that Borstan vary the meals, hoping Migi will learn to enjoy more than one favorite dish. Migi loves sweetglazed hog belly sandwiches and comes for lunch when the smokehouse fills with their sweet aroma. Borstan finds a way to honor his parents' request while keeping Migi fed. He crumbles the leftover crispy glazed cracklings into a savory seasoning that can be sprinkled over any dish. Behind Grommash Hold, the topping persuades Migi and his companions to pause their play and share lunch.

quest:97253.text:
Parts and Pieces. In Ratchet, Wrenix's machine lies in pieces after the pirates dismantled it. He sent it to face the raiders after five or six mercenaries failed to return alive. Now its scattered parts lie in the pirates' upper camp. Pirates along the coast south of Ratchet trouble the town's residents and tradesfolk. Wrenix the Wretched wanted to stop them without risking more coin on hired hands. Five or six mercenaries had already gone after the pirates and failed to return alive.

So Wrenix sent an automated machine to deal with the encampment on its own. He hoped the contraption could face the marauders without putting another living soul at risk. The pirates south of Ratchet proved resourceful. They used their curved scimitars as makeshift screwdrivers and pried Wrenix's machine apart before he could send instructions to retreat toward town.

Its delicate components now lie scattered in their upper camp. Wrenix needs someone to slip inside and gather five handfuls of the complicated parts from the dirt.

quest:97275.text: Whuut's the Rush. Yelmak sends you to carry a tonic to Whuut, whose eagerness has outrun his care. His apprentice reaches for rare herbs before learning what common plants can do. Whuut has a gift for alchemy, and the stirring rod comes naturally to him. Yet impatience leads him to spend the shop’s rarest reagents before he has mastered the basics. He reaches for legendary plants before learning how common herbs must be balanced, treating alchemy as a race. Yelmak answers his apprentice’s haste with a lesson in a vial. He brews a refined tonic from common speargrass and cattail using a quick method. Whuut is daydreaming about Black Lotus and Mountain Silversage when the tonic reaches his hands. Its simple ingredients show how much skill, patience, and respect for everyday plants can matter.

quest:97281.text: A Simmering Storm. In Durotar, the Dull Stormy Orb has caught Rezlak's attention. The goblin tinker sees reason to study the relic, recovered from the Dustwind harpies of Drygulch Ravine. Travelers who contend with the Dustwind harpies of Drygulch Ravine may find the Dull Stormy Orb among their strange trinkets. Its worn surface gives off a steady electrical vibration. Dark mist churns within, split now and then by sharp sparks. The relic shows the harpies have handled storm magic. Rezlak waits at the entrance to Drygulch Ravine, where the orb has caught his eye. Its discovery brings to mind advice from his employer, Chief Engineer Gazlowe of Ratchet. What the harpies meant to do with the miniature storm remains unknown. Now the orb is in goblin hands.

quest:97282.text: Stormy Potential. Near Drygulch Ravine, Rezlak looks for a way to protect his caravan from harpies. He hopes to charge a drained orb with the electrical organs of Durotar's thunder lizards. Near Drygulch Ravine in Durotar, harpies threaten Rezlak's caravan, and a sound magical orb has lost its power. Gazlowe, Ratchet's chief engineer, once advised Rezlak to seize opportunity when it knocks. Now the goblin plans to charge the dormant orb and answer both troubles at once. Rezlak needs strong electricity to restore his drained orb. Thunder lizards live in the gorge west of Drygulch Ravine, and their organs generate and conduct deadly lightning. He asks you to bring him those charged organs. Rezlak hopes to channel their volatile current into the orb and defend his supply wagons from harpy ambushes.

quest:97326.text: Rocks to Rests. Behind Grommash Hold, Thra and friends make room for games in Orgrimmar. They need smooth boulders to use as chairs and tables. Young orcs gather in a dirt clearing behind Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar. There they can play away from the fortress guards. The open ground suits their miniature figures, but with no furniture, they sit in the dust. Thra spots you passing and asks you to carry eight medium-sized, smooth boulders to the clearing. Their flat sides will make sturdy chairs and low tables. Then the youths can arrange their games without sitting in the dirt.

quest:97558.text: Hides for the Forsaken. In Tirisfal, the Forsaken gather hides to keep their bodies intact. Shelene Rhobart asks you to bring darkhound hides, duskbat wing membranes, and murloc skin. Forsaken flesh cannot mend itself. When they are wounded, the gap rots and stays open. So they stitch living tissue over their injuries to hold their forms together and keep their corpses working. Each kind of material mends a different part of the body. Thick darkhound hide holds firm over broad wounds. Duskbat wing membranes are thin and pliable, so they cover faces and fingers without stiffening them. Vile Fin murloc skin lines inner membranes and sensitive places such as cheeks and mouths.

quest:97891.text: Prompt Potion Runner. In Undercity, a runner carries Alessandro’s brew across the slime canal before it spoils. The delivery must reach the Apothecarium in time. Alessandro needs a swift courier in Undercity’s underground corridors. The Forsaken alchemist has made a volatile brew that will soon spoil. His undead joints are too frail for him to cross the toxic slime canal, so you carry it intact before it turns to useless sludge. Doctor Martin Felben waits at the Apothecarium for the brew, which he needs for his ongoing research. He says the six potions Alessandro sent before this one destabilized in transit. A timely delivery lets the doctor continue his shadowy experiments without interruption. The unstable brew and Alessandro’s frail joints show the hazards of Forsaken alchemy and undeath.

quest:97894.text: Business in Auberdine. In Stormwind, Borgus Steelhand waits for news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. You can reach Gorbold by sailing west from Stormwind Harbor to northern Kalimdor. Gorbold crossed the Great Sea to keep a merchant stall in auberdine. He hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without word, and Borgus worries for his brother so far from Ironforge and Stormwind. The passage to Kalimdor once led through Menethil Harbor or neutral goblin ports such as Booty Bay. Borgus sends you to the vessel at stormwind harbor's southern-most dock. Its direct sailing ends at Auberdine's long wooden piers.

quest:97914.text: Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine to Stormwind. He wants the settlement's work and its home known beyond Darkshore. Auberdine's sea passage now joins Darkshore directly to Stormwind. Its leaders want the shipping route kept safe and the coastal settlement linked to the wider Alliance. Nearby, the ruined cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran have long drawn more notice than Auberdine and its living people. Baros Alexston oversees Stormwind's construction and infrastructure. His duties include public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver's letter crosses the Great Sea to the official charged with the human capital's building needs.

quest:98021.text: Journey to Sentinel Hill. At Sentinel Hill, Journey to Sentinel Hill brings Alliance travelers into Westfall’s troubled farmlands. The local commanders have pleaded with Stormwind for months without answer, and now put any willing traveler to work. In Westfall, you arrive at Sentinel Hill, the outpost guarding the surrounding farmlands. Its garrison is short of soldiers and overlooked by the royal court. When travelers offer help, the local commander asks little about their standing. Any willing hands are welcome. For months, Sentinel Hill’s leaders have asked Stormwind for soldiers to defend Westfall from threats drawing near. With no reinforcements, local commanders accept whoever arrives. One commander expected an army and got a skinny elf instead. In Westfall, beggars cannot be choosers.

quest:98024.text: Journey to the Crossroads. A newly arrived traveler from the elemental plane is sent to the Crossroads in the Barrens. There, Thork calls for aid as the Horde faces the dangers of Kalimdor's frontier. You have come to Azeroth from the elemental plane. Mortal conflicts may seem small beside what you have known, but the Horde faces dangers of its own. Service on the frontier gives you a chance to grow formidable while aiding the realm. The Barrens lie southwest, and the Crossroads stands among its broad, sun-baked plains. This Horde outpost is a vital junction, though dangers press its defenders from every side. Report to Thork and join the settlement's defense.

quest:98025.text: WANTED: Jai'vhanel. Near Auberdine, Jai'vhanel ambushes travelers on the coastal roads. The Auberdine Village Council has set a bounty for her death near the ruins of Ameth'Aran, with proof to be brought to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea. On Darkshore's coastal roads near Auberdine, travelers face danger from a mad owl. Jai'vhanel, known locally as Swordfeather, has turned on those who pass. She ambushes travelers and couriers near the settlement, leaving the roads unsafe. The Auberdine Village Council offers a bounty to make the roads safer. Jai'vhanel hunts north of the ruins of Ameth'Aran, along the mountain base. Bring one of her black feathers to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine as proof of the kill and to claim the reward.

quest:98042.text: It's All Fun and Games Until.... Thundris hears a troubled report and examines the discovery brought before him. Its mark sends the relic to Darnassus for study. You bring a troubling discovery to Thundris and seek his counsel. He listens to your report and examines what you have brought. Then he falls quiet, for the signs before him are too dark to dismiss.

quest:98046.text: Crown of the Earth. In Darnassus, Fandral Staghelm turns from a failed rite and sends its vessel away. He asks you to carry it to Priestess Lariia at the Temple of the Moon for disposal. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm guides the night elves while Malfurion Stormrage is absent. Seeking answers, he performs an incantation with sacred water held in a phial. The rite brings no answer, and Fandral's temper rises. Certain the water is useless, he dismisses you with sharp words and sends you south to the Temple of the Moon, where the priestesses can dispose of the vessel.

quest:98065.text: Crown of the Earth. Within Darnassus, purified Moonwell Remnants are brought to High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. The meeting takes place in the Temple of the Moon, where the waters’ sacred meaning meets the strain between Tyrande and Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Once the sacred Moonwell Remnants are collected, you pour the blessed water into a ceremonial vessel and carry it to Tyrande Whisperwind. The High Priestess of Elune keeps audience high within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. She watches over the city and offers her goddess’s light to all who enter. To place sacred water in her care is an honor and an act of devotion to Elune.

quest:98067.text: Eyes of the Sentinels. In Darnassus, Sentinel Dalia Sunblade sets owls to watch as unease grows across Teldrassil. Their posts guard the city and leave the Sentinels time to pray to Elune. At the Temple of the Moon, Sentinel Dalia Sunblade watches over Darnassus. General Shandris Feathermoon has decreed that every warrior must balance skill in battle with devotion to Elune. So Dalia arranges for sentinel owls to watch key places in the city. Their daily duties leave the Sentinels time for prayer and reflection before the Moon Goddess, while Darnassus remains guarded. Unease spreads across Teldrassil, and the Sentinels grow more watchful. Sentinel owls take posts at the northern entrance to the depths beneath Cenarion Hold, the bank in the town square, the inn in Craftsman's Terrace, and the main city gates. Local city guards help place them. From these posts, the owls watch over those who walk the streets of the Great Tree.

quest:982.text: Deep Ocean, Vast Sea. North of Auberdine, two night elf vessels lie beneath the waves. Murlocs ambushed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as they sailed into port, and the surviving crews seek a way to mourn their lost captains. Murlocs overwhelmed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as they neared Auberdine. Both ships sank in the shallows north of the settlement. Their surviving crews reached shore, but the loss of the vessels and their captains still weighs on the port. Gorbold Steelhand, a dwarf in Auberdine, seeks to honor the fallen night elf captains. Murlocs now occupy the underwater wrecks, though the captains' lockboxes remain in the flooded holds. Their logs and personal effects could help the surviving sailors mourn their commanders and lay their spirits to rest.

quest:98247.text: Shipping Label. A damaged Shipping Label leads you to the Azeroth Commerce Authority's trade hub at Three Corners in the Redridge Mountains. It marks a supply crate as the authority's property and shows where to report it. A damaged label marks a stocked supply crate as freight belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. The destination and recipient are torn away. Anyone who finds the cargo can return it or report it to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rough map shows the roads toward the Three Corners intersection. At Three Corners, representatives of the Azeroth Commerce Authority enlist travelers as independent couriers. The authority asks no strict merchant contracts of its haulers. Instead, it runs an informal network and gives Merchant's Favor to couriers who recover missing cargo or complete abandoned deliveries along the highway.

quest:98298.text: Arugal's Folly. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks the truth behind the worgen near the Greymane Wall. He hopes their remains will prove that Archmage Arugal bound the beasts but did not bring their curse into being. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Forsaken mage Dalar Dawnweaver means to strip away the mystery around his rival, Archmage Arugal. Enchanted shackles show that Arugal lacked the power to summon or create the worgen packs terrorizing the region. His magic could only hold the beasts for a time. How the affliction began remains unknown. Dalar sends you south to the Greymane Wall for proof. Feral worgen attack and infect nearby human populations in the wilderness around its imposing fortifications. You can bring Dalar physical evidence by killing the beasts and gathering pieces of their bodies. He needs those samples to study the affliction's nature.

quest:98386.text: Alther's Mill. At Alther's Mill, giant spiders have stopped the timber shipments Lakeshire needs for its bridge. Foreman Oslow is waiting for the lumber so the work can continue. Foreman Oslow is trying to keep Lakeshire's bridge repairs on schedule. Blackrock orcs, gnoll packs, and murlocs along Lake Everstill already strain his workforce. Now giant tarantulas have overrun Alther's Mill to the east, stopping the timber shipments the bridge needs. Greater tarantulas lurk among the timber stacks, leaving Alther's Mill useless.
